**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the dawn, and by ten nights, and by the even and the odd, and by the night when it passes, is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾**

This is an oath. Our Lord, exalted is His praise, swore by the dawn, which is the dawn of morning.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) differed about what is meant by it. Some said it refers to the day.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aghharr al-Minqari, from Khalifah ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿By the dawn﴾: he said, "The day."

Others said it refers to the dawn prayer.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿By the dawn﴾: he meant the dawn prayer.

Others said it is the dawn of morning.

Those who said that:

- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿By the dawn﴾: he said, "The dawn: the dawn of morning."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, that he said: ﴿By the dawn﴾: "The dawn is an oath which God swore by."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and by ten nights﴾:

The people of ta'wil differed about which nights these ten are. Some said: they are the ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy, 'Abd al-Wahhab and Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from 'Awf, from Zurarah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The ten nights by which God swore are the first ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and ten nights﴾: "the ten of al-Adha (the Sacrifice)." He said: "It is also said: the ten are the first of the year, from Muharram."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr: ﴿and ten nights﴾: "from the beginning of Dhu al-Hijjah until the day of sacrifice."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Awf informed us, saying: Zurarah ibn Awfa related to us, saying: Ibn Abbas said: "The ten nights by which God swore are the first nights of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of Dhu al-Hijjah, which are those for which God appointed Musa (ﷺ)."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aghharr al-Minqari, from Khalifah ibn Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of al-Adha."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "We used to be told that they are the ten of al-Adha."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, who said: "No deed in the nights of the year is more virtuous than it is in the nights of the ten, and they are the ten of Musa, which God completed for him."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, who said: "The nights of the ten: they are the most virtuous days of the year."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿and ten nights﴾: "That is, the ten of al-Adha."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and ten nights﴾: "The first of Dhu al-Hijjah"; and he said: "They are the ten of Muharram from its beginning."

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that they are the ten of al-Adha, due to the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars of ta'wil upon it. And 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani related to me, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab related to me, saying: 'Ayyash ibn 'Uqbah informed me, saying: Jubayr ibn Nu'aym related to me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "﴿By the dawn, and ten nights﴾: the ten of al-Adha."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the even and the odd, and the night when it passes, is there in that an oath﴾:

The people of ta'wil differed about what is meant by the odd in His saying ﴿and the odd﴾. Some said: the even is the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), and the odd is the day of 'Arafah.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy, 'Abd al-Wahhab and Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from 'Awf, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The odd is the day of 'Arafah, and the even is the day of slaughter."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Awf informed us, saying: Zurarah ibn Awfa related to us, saying: Ibn Abbas said: "The even: the day of sacrifice; and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, who said: 'Ikrimah said, from Ibn Abbas: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- He related it to us again another time, and said: "The even: the days of sacrifice," and the rest of the narration is like it.
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿the even﴾: "The day of sacrifice"; ﴿and the odd﴾: "The day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from 'Ikrimah, who said: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- He said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Sinan, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿and ten nights and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "God swore by them because of what He knows of their virtue over the other days; and the better of these two days, because of what is known of their virtue over the other nights ﴿and the even and the odd﴾." He said: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "'Ikrimah used to say: The even: the day of al-Adha, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: 'Ikrimah said: "'Arafah is odd, and the sacrifice is even; 'Arafah is the ninth day, and the sacrifice is the tenth day."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿the even﴾: "The day of sacrifice," ﴿and the odd﴾: "The day of 'Arafah."

Others said: the even is the two days after the day of sacrifice, and the odd is the third day.

Those who said that:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: "The even: two days after the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of the final departure (al-nafr al-akhir)," as God says: ﴿Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾.

Others said: the even is all creation, and the odd is God.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: "God is the odd, and you are the even." It is also said: "The even: the dawn prayer, and the odd: the sunset prayer (maghrib)."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "Every creature of God is even: the heaven and the earth, the land and the sea, the jinn and mankind, the sun and the moon; and God alone is the odd."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Mujahid said regarding His saying ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾: "Disbelief and faith, happiness and misery, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, jinn and mankind; and the odd is God." He said: "And he said regarding the even and the odd the same."
- 'Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid related to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "God created pairs of everything, and God is the one odd, the eternal (samad)."
- Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "The even: the pair; and the odd: God."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "The odd is God, and whatever God created of things is even."

Others said: it refers to creation, because all creation is even and odd.

- He said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "All creation is even and odd, and He swore by creation."
- He said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said regarding that: "All creation is even." ﴿and the even and the odd﴾. He said: "My father used to say: everything God created is even and odd, so He swore by what He created, and He swore by what you see and what you do not see."

Others said: rather, it refers to the obligatory prayers, of which some are even, such as the dawn and noon prayers, and some are odd, such as the sunset prayer.

Those who said that:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "'Imran ibn Husayn used to say: ﴿the even and the odd﴾: the prayer."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: "'Imran said: they are the obligatory prayers, in which there is the even and the odd."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "That is the sunset prayer. The even: two rak'ahs, and the odd: the third rak'ah." And some of them traced the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn to the Prophet.

Those who said that:

- Nasr ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: my father related to me, saying: Khalid ibn Qays related to me, from Qatadah, from 'Imran ibn 'Isam, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the even and the odd, that he said: "It is the prayer: of it is the even, and of it is the odd."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, that he was asked about the even and the odd, and he said: "'Imran ibn 'Isam al-Dab'i informed me, from a shaykh from the people of Basra, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: ﴿the even and the odd﴾: 'It is the prayer: of it is the even, and of it is the odd.'"
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Hammam ibn Yahya informed us, from 'Imran ibn 'Isam, from a shaykh from the people of Basra, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said regarding this verse ﴿the even and the odd﴾: "It is the prayer: of it is the even, and of it is the odd."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿the even and the odd﴾: "Indeed, of the prayer there is an even, and indeed of it there is an odd."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, that he was asked about the even and the odd, and he said: "al-Hasan said: it is the number." A report from the Prophet (ﷺ) supporting the view we mentioned from Abu al-Zubayr has also been transmitted.

Those who said that:

- 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani related to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab related to us, saying: 'Ayyash ibn 'Uqbah informed me, saying: Jubayr ibn Nu'aym related to me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The even: the two days; and the odd: the one day."

The correct view on this matter is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, swore by the even and the odd, and He did not specify one type of even or odd over another by any report or by reason. Every even and every odd is among what He swore by, according to what the people of ta'wil said, that it is included in His oath because of the generality of His swearing by it.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying ﴿and the odd (al-witr)﴾. The majority of reciters of Medina, Mecca and Basra, and some reciters of Kufa, read it with a kasra on the waw (al-witr).

The correct view on this matter is that both are well-known, widely transmitted recitations among the reciters of the regions, and two well-known dialects among the Arabs, so whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾:

He says: "and the night when it moves on and departs." From this one says: "So-and-so traveled by night (sara fulan laylan yasri)" when he traveled.

Some said: what is meant by His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾ is the night of Jam' (Muzdalifah), which is the night of Muzdalifah.

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we said in this.

Those who said that:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: "until it takes away some of it from the rest."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he says: "when it departs."
- Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "when it travels."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "and the night when it travels."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he says: "when it travels."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "when it travels."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "The night when it moves."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "the night of Jam'."

The reciters differed in the recitation of this. The majority of reciters of Syria and Iraq read ﴿yasri﴾ without a ya'. Some reciters read it with the ya' retained, and omitting the ya' in this is more pleasing to us, so that the verse-endings (ru'us al-ayy) agree, since they end in the letter ra'. The Arabs sometimes drop the ya' in the nominative position in such cases, relying on the kasra of the letter before it, as in the saying of the poet:

*My wealth does not stay hidden for a single day,*
*and indeed my poverty conceals my character.*[[The people of qadar are the deniers of qadar, not its affirmers. The advocates of tafwid (delegation) are the Qadariyyah, the Mu'tazilah and the Imamiyyah. They claim that the matter was delegated (i.e., referred back) to the human being, so that his will suffices to bring his act into existence, whether it is obedience or disobedience, and that he is the creator of his acts, and that choice is in his hand.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿is there in that an oath for one of intellect﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Is there in what I have sworn by of these matters a sufficient proof for one of intellect?" What is meant by it is: in this oath there is a sufficiency for whoever understands from his Lord, of what is weightier than it in swearing. As for the meaning of His saying ﴿for one of intellect (li-dhi hijr)﴾: it means "for one of reason and sound mind." It is said of a man, when he is master of himself, restraining it and controlling it: "He is one of hijr (restraint)," and from this comes the saying: "al-hakim hajara 'ala fulan (the judge placed fulan under restraint)."

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we said in this.

Those who said that:

- Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, both saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan informed us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿for one of intellect (li-dhi hijr)﴾: he said: "For one of insight (nuha) and intellect."
- 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿for one of intellect﴾: he said: "For those of insight (uli al-nuha)."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿is there in that an oath for one of intellect﴾: he said: "One of hijr, nuha and intellect."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿an oath for one of intellect﴾: he said: "For one of intellect, for one of nuha."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 89, verse 1–5 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aghurr al-Minqari, from Khalifa ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Is there not in this an oath for one of intellect?﴾ He said: for one who has understanding (lubb), for one who has reason (hijā).

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect (hijr)?﴾ He said: for one who has reason (aql).

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: for one who has reason, for one who has opinion.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Umara narrated to me, he said: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Israil informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾ He said: for one who has understanding (lubb), or restraint (nuha).

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to us, he said: Khalaf ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿an oath for one of intellect﴾ He said: for one who has reason.

⁕ Yaqub narrated to me, he said: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾ He said: for one who has forbearance (hilm).

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mamar, from Qatada, regarding his saying: ﴿for one of intellect﴾ He said: for one who has reason (hijā); and al-Hasan said: for one who has understanding (lubb).

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding his saying: ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾ For one who has reason (hijā), for one who has intellect and understanding (lubb).

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his saying: ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾ He said: for one who has reason, and he recited: ﴿for a people who reason (ya'qilun)﴾ and ﴿for those of understanding (li-ulil-albab)﴾, and they are those whom God rebuked; and he said: intellect (aql) and understanding (lubb) are one, except that they differ in the speech of the Arabs.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the dawn, and by ten nights, and by the even and the odd, and by the night when it passes, is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾**

This is an oath. Our Lord, exalted is His praise, swore by the dawn, which is the dawn of morning.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) differed about what is meant by it. Some said it refers to the day.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aghharr al-Minqari, from Khalifah ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿By the dawn﴾: he said, "The day."

Others said it refers to the dawn prayer.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿By the dawn﴾: he meant the dawn prayer.

Others said it is the dawn of morning.

Those who said that:

- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿By the dawn﴾: he said, "The dawn: the dawn of morning."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, that he said: ﴿By the dawn﴾: "The dawn is an oath which God swore by."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and by ten nights﴾:

The people of ta'wil differed about which nights these ten are. Some said: they are the ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy, 'Abd al-Wahhab and Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from 'Awf, from Zurarah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The ten nights by which God swore are the first ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and ten nights﴾: "the ten of al-Adha (the Sacrifice)." He said: "It is also said: the ten are the first of the year, from Muharram."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr: ﴿and ten nights﴾: "from the beginning of Dhu al-Hijjah until the day of sacrifice."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Awf informed us, saying: Zurarah ibn Awfa related to us, saying: Ibn Abbas said: "The ten nights by which God swore are the first nights of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of Dhu al-Hijjah, which are those for which God appointed Musa (ﷺ)."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aghharr al-Minqari, from Khalifah ibn Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of al-Adha."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "We used to be told that they are the ten of al-Adha."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, who said: "No deed in the nights of the year is more virtuous than it is in the nights of the ten, and they are the ten of Musa, which God completed for him."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, who said: "The nights of the ten: they are the most virtuous days of the year."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿and ten nights﴾: "That is, the ten of al-Adha."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and ten nights﴾: "The first of Dhu al-Hijjah"; and he said: "They are the ten of Muharram from its beginning."

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that they are the ten of al-Adha, due to the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars of ta'wil upon it. And 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani related to me, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab related to me, saying: 'Ayyash ibn 'Uqbah informed me, saying: Jubayr ibn Nu'aym related to me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "﴿By the dawn, and ten nights﴾: the ten of al-Adha."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the even and the odd, and the night when it passes, is there in that an oath﴾:

The people of ta'wil differed about what is meant by the odd in His saying ﴿and the odd﴾. Some said: the even is the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), and the odd is the day of 'Arafah.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy, 'Abd al-Wahhab and Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from 'Awf, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The odd is the day of 'Arafah, and the even is the day of slaughter."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Awf informed us, saying: Zurarah ibn Awfa related to us, saying: Ibn Abbas said: "The even: the day of sacrifice; and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, who said: 'Ikrimah said, from Ibn Abbas: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- He related it to us again another time, and said: "The even: the days of sacrifice," and the rest of the narration is like it.
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿the even﴾: "The day of sacrifice"; ﴿and the odd﴾: "The day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from 'Ikrimah, who said: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- He said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Sinan, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿and ten nights and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "God swore by them because of what He knows of their virtue over the other days; and the better of these two days, because of what is known of their virtue over the other nights ﴿and the even and the odd﴾." He said: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "'Ikrimah used to say: The even: the day of al-Adha, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: 'Ikrimah said: "'Arafah is odd, and the sacrifice is even; 'Arafah is the ninth day, and the sacrifice is the tenth day."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿the even﴾: "The day of sacrifice," ﴿and the odd﴾: "The day of 'Arafah."

Others said: the even is the two days after the day of sacrifice, and the odd is the third day.

Those who said that:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: "The even: two days after the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of the final departure (al-nafr al-akhir)," as God says: ﴿Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾.

Others said: the even is all creation, and the odd is God.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: "God is the odd, and you are the even." It is also said: "The even: the dawn prayer, and the odd: the sunset prayer (maghrib)."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "Every creature of God is even: the heaven and the earth, the land and the sea, the jinn and mankind, the sun and the moon; and God alone is the odd."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Mujahid said regarding His saying ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾: "Disbelief and faith, happiness and misery, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, jinn and mankind; and the odd is God." He said: "And he said regarding the even and the odd the same."
- 'Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid related to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "God created pairs of everything, and God is the one odd, the eternal (samad)."
- Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "The even: the pair; and the odd: God."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "The odd is God, and whatever God created of things is even."

Others said: it refers to creation, because all creation is even and odd.

- He said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "All creation is even and odd, and He swore by creation."
- He said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said regarding that: "All creation is even." ﴿and the even and the odd﴾. He said: "My father used to say: everything God created is even and odd, so He swore by what He created, and He swore by what you see and what you do not see."

Others said: rather, it refers to the obligatory prayers, of which some are even, such as the dawn and noon prayers, and some are odd, such as the sunset prayer.

Those who said that:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "'Imran ibn Husayn used to say: ﴿the even and the odd﴾: the prayer."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: "'Imran said: they are the obligatory prayers, in which there is the even and the odd."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "That is the sunset prayer. The even: two rak'ahs, and the odd: the third rak'ah." And some of them traced the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn to the Prophet.

Those who said that:

- Nasr ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: my father related to me, saying: Khalid ibn Qays related to me, from Qatadah, from 'Imran ibn 'Isam, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the even and the odd, that he said: "It is the prayer: of it is the even, and of it is the odd."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, that he was asked about the even and the odd, and he said: "'Imran ibn 'Isam al-Dab'i informed me, from a shaykh from the people of Basra, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: ﴿the even and the odd﴾: 'It is the prayer: of it is the even, and of it is the odd.'"
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Hammam ibn Yahya informed us, from 'Imran ibn 'Isam, from a shaykh from the people of Basra, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said regarding this verse ﴿the even and the odd﴾: "It is the prayer: of it is the even, and of it is the odd."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿the even and the odd﴾: "Indeed, of the prayer there is an even, and indeed of it there is an odd."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, that he was asked about the even and the odd, and he said: "al-Hasan said: it is the number." A report from the Prophet (ﷺ) supporting the view we mentioned from Abu al-Zubayr has also been transmitted.

Those who said that:

- 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani related to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab related to us, saying: 'Ayyash ibn 'Uqbah informed me, saying: Jubayr ibn Nu'aym related to me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The even: the two days; and the odd: the one day."

The correct view on this matter is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, swore by the even and the odd, and He did not specify one type of even or odd over another by any report or by reason. Every even and every odd is among what He swore by, according to what the people of ta'wil said, that it is included in His oath because of the generality of His swearing by it.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying ﴿and the odd (al-witr)﴾. The majority of reciters of Medina, Mecca and Basra, and some reciters of Kufa, read it with a kasra on the waw (al-witr).

The correct view on this matter is that both are well-known, widely transmitted recitations among the reciters of the regions, and two well-known dialects among the Arabs, so whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾:

He says: "and the night when it moves on and departs." From this one says: "So-and-so traveled by night (sara fulan laylan yasri)" when he traveled.

Some said: what is meant by His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾ is the night of Jam' (Muzdalifah), which is the night of Muzdalifah.

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we said in this.

Those who said that:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: "until it takes away some of it from the rest."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he says: "when it departs."
- Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "when it travels."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "and the night when it travels."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he says: "when it travels."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "when it travels."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "The night when it moves."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "the night of Jam'."

The reciters differed in the recitation of this. The majority of reciters of Syria and Iraq read ﴿yasri﴾ without a ya'. Some reciters read it with the ya' retained, and omitting the ya' in this is more pleasing to us, so that the verse-endings (ru'us al-ayy) agree, since they end in the letter ra'. The Arabs sometimes drop the ya' in the nominative position in such cases, relying on the kasra of the letter before it, as in the saying of the poet:

*My wealth does not stay hidden for a single day,*
*and indeed my poverty conceals my character.*[[The people of qadar are the deniers of qadar, not its affirmers. The advocates of tafwid (delegation) are the Qadariyyah, the Mu'tazilah and the Imamiyyah. They claim that the matter was delegated (i.e., referred back) to the human being, so that his will suffices to bring his act into existence, whether it is obedience or disobedience, and that he is the creator of his acts, and that choice is in his hand.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿is there in that an oath for one of intellect﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Is there in what I have sworn by of these matters a sufficient proof for one of intellect?" What is meant by it is: in this oath there is a sufficiency for whoever understands from his Lord, of what is weightier than it in swearing. As for the meaning of His saying ﴿for one of intellect (li-dhi hijr)﴾: it means "for one of reason and sound mind." It is said of a man, when he is master of himself, restraining it and controlling it: "He is one of hijr (restraint)," and from this comes the saying: "al-hakim hajara 'ala fulan (the judge placed fulan under restraint)."

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we said in this.

Those who said that:

- Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, both saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan informed us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿for one of intellect (li-dhi hijr)﴾: he said: "For one of insight (nuha) and intellect."
- 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿for one of intellect﴾: he said: "For those of insight (uli al-nuha)."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿is there in that an oath for one of intellect﴾: he said: "One of hijr, nuha and intellect."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿an oath for one of intellect﴾: he said: "For one of intellect, for one of nuha."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 89, verse 1–5 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aghurr al-Minqari, from Khalifa ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Is there not in this an oath for one of intellect?﴾ He said: for one who has understanding (lubb), for one who has reason (hijā).

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect (hijr)?﴾ He said: for one who has reason (aql).

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: for one who has reason, for one who has opinion.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Umara narrated to me, he said: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Israil informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾ He said: for one who has understanding (lubb), or restraint (nuha).

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to us, he said: Khalaf ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿an oath for one of intellect﴾ He said: for one who has reason.

⁕ Yaqub narrated to me, he said: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾ He said: for one who has forbearance (hilm).

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mamar, from Qatada, regarding his saying: ﴿for one of intellect﴾ He said: for one who has reason (hijā); and al-Hasan said: for one who has understanding (lubb).

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding his saying: ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾ For one who has reason (hijā), for one who has intellect and understanding (lubb).

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his saying: ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾ He said: for one who has reason, and he recited: ﴿for a people who reason (ya'qilun)﴾ and ﴿for those of understanding (li-ulil-albab)﴾, and they are those whom God rebuked; and he said: intellect (aql) and understanding (lubb) are one, except that they differ in the speech of the Arabs.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the dawn, and by ten nights, and by the even and the odd, and by the night when it passes, is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾**

This is an oath. Our Lord, exalted is His praise, swore by the dawn, which is the dawn of morning.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) differed about what is meant by it. Some said it refers to the day.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aghharr al-Minqari, from Khalifah ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿By the dawn﴾: he said, "The day."

Others said it refers to the dawn prayer.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿By the dawn﴾: he meant the dawn prayer.

Others said it is the dawn of morning.

Those who said that:

- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿By the dawn﴾: he said, "The dawn: the dawn of morning."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, that he said: ﴿By the dawn﴾: "The dawn is an oath which God swore by."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and by ten nights﴾:

The people of ta'wil differed about which nights these ten are. Some said: they are the ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy, 'Abd al-Wahhab and Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from 'Awf, from Zurarah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The ten nights by which God swore are the first ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and ten nights﴾: "the ten of al-Adha (the Sacrifice)." He said: "It is also said: the ten are the first of the year, from Muharram."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr: ﴿and ten nights﴾: "from the beginning of Dhu al-Hijjah until the day of sacrifice."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Awf informed us, saying: Zurarah ibn Awfa related to us, saying: Ibn Abbas said: "The ten nights by which God swore are the first nights of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of Dhu al-Hijjah, which are those for which God appointed Musa (ﷺ)."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aghharr al-Minqari, from Khalifah ibn Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of al-Adha."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "We used to be told that they are the ten of al-Adha."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, who said: "No deed in the nights of the year is more virtuous than it is in the nights of the ten, and they are the ten of Musa, which God completed for him."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, who said: "The nights of the ten: they are the most virtuous days of the year."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿and ten nights﴾: "That is, the ten of al-Adha."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and ten nights﴾: "The first of Dhu al-Hijjah"; and he said: "They are the ten of Muharram from its beginning."

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that they are the ten of al-Adha, due to the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars of ta'wil upon it. And 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani related to me, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab related to me, saying: 'Ayyash ibn 'Uqbah informed me, saying: Jubayr ibn Nu'aym related to me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "﴿By the dawn, and ten nights﴾: the ten of al-Adha."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the even and the odd, and the night when it passes, is there in that an oath﴾:

The people of ta'wil differed about what is meant by the odd in His saying ﴿and the odd﴾. Some said: the even is the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), and the odd is the day of 'Arafah.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy, 'Abd al-Wahhab and Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from 'Awf, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The odd is the day of 'Arafah, and the even is the day of slaughter."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Awf informed us, saying: Zurarah ibn Awfa related to us, saying: Ibn Abbas said: "The even: the day of sacrifice; and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, who said: 'Ikrimah said, from Ibn Abbas: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- He related it to us again another time, and said: "The even: the days of sacrifice," and the rest of the narration is like it.
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿the even﴾: "The day of sacrifice"; ﴿and the odd﴾: "The day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from 'Ikrimah, who said: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- He said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Sinan, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿and ten nights and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "God swore by them because of what He knows of their virtue over the other days; and the better of these two days, because of what is known of their virtue over the other nights ﴿and the even and the odd﴾." He said: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "'Ikrimah used to say: The even: the day of al-Adha, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: 'Ikrimah said: "'Arafah is odd, and the sacrifice is even; 'Arafah is the ninth day, and the sacrifice is the tenth day."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿the even﴾: "The day of sacrifice," ﴿and the odd﴾: "The day of 'Arafah."

Others said: the even is the two days after the day of sacrifice, and the odd is the third day.

Those who said that:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: "The even: two days after the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of the final departure (al-nafr al-akhir)," as God says: ﴿Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾.

Others said: the even is all creation, and the odd is God.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: "God is the odd, and you are the even." It is also said: "The even: the dawn prayer, and the odd: the sunset prayer (maghrib)."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "Every creature of God is even: the heaven and the earth, the land and the sea, the jinn and mankind, the sun and the moon; and God alone is the odd."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Mujahid said regarding His saying ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾: "Disbelief and faith, happiness and misery, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, jinn and mankind; and the odd is God." He said: "And he said regarding the even and the odd the same."
- 'Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid related to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "God created pairs of everything, and God is the one odd, the eternal (samad)."
- Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "The even: the pair; and the odd: God."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "The odd is God, and whatever God created of things is even."

Others said: it refers to creation, because all creation is even and odd.

- He said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "All creation is even and odd, and He swore by creation."
- He said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said regarding that: "All creation is even." ﴿and the even and the odd﴾. He said: "My father used to say: everything God created is even and odd, so He swore by what He created, and He swore by what you see and what you do not see."

Others said: rather, it refers to the obligatory prayers, of which some are even, such as the dawn and noon prayers, and some are odd, such as the sunset prayer.

Those who said that:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "'Imran ibn Husayn used to say: ﴿the even and the odd﴾: the prayer."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: "'Imran said: they are the obligatory prayers, in which there is the even and the odd."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "That is the sunset prayer. The even: two rak'ahs, and the odd: the third rak'ah." And some of them traced the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn to the Prophet.

Those who said that:

- Nasr ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: my father related to me, saying: Khalid ibn Qays related to me, from Qatadah, from 'Imran ibn 'Isam, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the even and the odd, that he said: "It is the prayer: of it is the even, and of it is the odd."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, that he was asked about the even and the odd, and he said: "'Imran ibn 'Isam al-Dab'i informed me, from a shaykh from the people of Basra, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: ﴿the even and the odd﴾: 'It is the prayer: of it is the even, and of it is the odd.'"
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Hammam ibn Yahya informed us, from 'Imran ibn 'Isam, from a shaykh from the people of Basra, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said regarding this verse ﴿the even and the odd﴾: "It is the prayer: of it is the even, and of it is the odd."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿the even and the odd﴾: "Indeed, of the prayer there is an even, and indeed of it there is an odd."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, that he was asked about the even and the odd, and he said: "al-Hasan said: it is the number." A report from the Prophet (ﷺ) supporting the view we mentioned from Abu al-Zubayr has also been transmitted.

Those who said that:

- 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani related to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab related to us, saying: 'Ayyash ibn 'Uqbah informed me, saying: Jubayr ibn Nu'aym related to me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The even: the two days; and the odd: the one day."

The correct view on this matter is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, swore by the even and the odd, and He did not specify one type of even or odd over another by any report or by reason. Every even and every odd is among what He swore by, according to what the people of ta'wil said, that it is included in His oath because of the generality of His swearing by it.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying ﴿and the odd (al-witr)﴾. The majority of reciters of Medina, Mecca and Basra, and some reciters of Kufa, read it with a kasra on the waw (al-witr).

The correct view on this matter is that both are well-known, widely transmitted recitations among the reciters of the regions, and two well-known dialects among the Arabs, so whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾:

He says: "and the night when it moves on and departs." From this one says: "So-and-so traveled by night (sara fulan laylan yasri)" when he traveled.

Some said: what is meant by His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾ is the night of Jam' (Muzdalifah), which is the night of Muzdalifah.

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we said in this.

Those who said that:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: "until it takes away some of it from the rest."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he says: "when it departs."
- Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "when it travels."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "and the night when it travels."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he says: "when it travels."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "when it travels."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "The night when it moves."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "the night of Jam'."

The reciters differed in the recitation of this. The majority of reciters of Syria and Iraq read ﴿yasri﴾ without a ya'. Some reciters read it with the ya' retained, and omitting the ya' in this is more pleasing to us, so that the verse-endings (ru'us al-ayy) agree, since they end in the letter ra'. The Arabs sometimes drop the ya' in the nominative position in such cases, relying on the kasra of the letter before it, as in the saying of the poet:

*My wealth does not stay hidden for a single day,*
*and indeed my poverty conceals my character.*[[The people of qadar are the deniers of qadar, not its affirmers. The advocates of tafwid (delegation) are the Qadariyyah, the Mu'tazilah and the Imamiyyah. They claim that the matter was delegated (i.e., referred back) to the human being, so that his will suffices to bring his act into existence, whether it is obedience or disobedience, and that he is the creator of his acts, and that choice is in his hand.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿is there in that an oath for one of intellect﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Is there in what I have sworn by of these matters a sufficient proof for one of intellect?" What is meant by it is: in this oath there is a sufficiency for whoever understands from his Lord, of what is weightier than it in swearing. As for the meaning of His saying ﴿for one of intellect (li-dhi hijr)﴾: it means "for one of reason and sound mind." It is said of a man, when he is master of himself, restraining it and controlling it: "He is one of hijr (restraint)," and from this comes the saying: "al-hakim hajara 'ala fulan (the judge placed fulan under restraint)."

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we said in this.

Those who said that:

- Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, both saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan informed us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿for one of intellect (li-dhi hijr)﴾: he said: "For one of insight (nuha) and intellect."
- 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿for one of intellect﴾: he said: "For those of insight (uli al-nuha)."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿is there in that an oath for one of intellect﴾: he said: "One of hijr, nuha and intellect."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿an oath for one of intellect﴾: he said: "For one of intellect, for one of nuha."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 89, verse 1–5 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aghurr al-Minqari, from Khalifa ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Is there not in this an oath for one of intellect?﴾ He said: for one who has understanding (lubb), for one who has reason (hijā).

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect (hijr)?﴾ He said: for one who has reason (aql).

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: for one who has reason, for one who has opinion.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Umara narrated to me, he said: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Israil informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾ He said: for one who has understanding (lubb), or restraint (nuha).

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to us, he said: Khalaf ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿an oath for one of intellect﴾ He said: for one who has reason.

⁕ Yaqub narrated to me, he said: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾ He said: for one who has forbearance (hilm).

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mamar, from Qatada, regarding his saying: ﴿for one of intellect﴾ He said: for one who has reason (hijā); and al-Hasan said: for one who has understanding (lubb).

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding his saying: ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾ For one who has reason (hijā), for one who has intellect and understanding (lubb).

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his saying: ﴿Is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾ He said: for one who has reason, and he recited: ﴿for a people who reason (ya'qilun)﴾ and ﴿for those of understanding (li-ulil-albab)﴾, and they are those whom God rebuked; and he said: intellect (aql) and understanding (lubb) are one, except that they differ in the speech of the Arabs.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the dawn, and by ten nights, and by the even and the odd, and by the night when it passes, is there in that an oath for one of intellect?﴾**

This is an oath. Our Lord, exalted is His praise, swore by the dawn, which is the dawn of morning.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) differed about what is meant by it. Some said it refers to the day.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aghharr al-Minqari, from Khalifah ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿By the dawn﴾: he said, "The day."

Others said it refers to the dawn prayer.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿By the dawn﴾: he meant the dawn prayer.

Others said it is the dawn of morning.

Those who said that:

- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿By the dawn﴾: he said, "The dawn: the dawn of morning."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, that he said: ﴿By the dawn﴾: "The dawn is an oath which God swore by."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and by ten nights﴾:

The people of ta'wil differed about which nights these ten are. Some said: they are the ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy, 'Abd al-Wahhab and Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from 'Awf, from Zurarah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The ten nights by which God swore are the first ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and ten nights﴾: "the ten of al-Adha (the Sacrifice)." He said: "It is also said: the ten are the first of the year, from Muharram."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr: ﴿and ten nights﴾: "from the beginning of Dhu al-Hijjah until the day of sacrifice."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Awf informed us, saying: Zurarah ibn Awfa related to us, saying: Ibn Abbas said: "The ten nights by which God swore are the first nights of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of Dhu al-Hijjah, which are those for which God appointed Musa (ﷺ)."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aghharr al-Minqari, from Khalifah ibn Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of al-Adha."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "The ten of Dhu al-Hijjah."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and ten nights﴾: he said: "We used to be told that they are the ten of al-Adha."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, who said: "No deed in the nights of the year is more virtuous than it is in the nights of the ten, and they are the ten of Musa, which God completed for him."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, who said: "The nights of the ten: they are the most virtuous days of the year."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿and ten nights﴾: "That is, the ten of al-Adha."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and ten nights﴾: "The first of Dhu al-Hijjah"; and he said: "They are the ten of Muharram from its beginning."

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that they are the ten of al-Adha, due to the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars of ta'wil upon it. And 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani related to me, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab related to me, saying: 'Ayyash ibn 'Uqbah informed me, saying: Jubayr ibn Nu'aym related to me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "﴿By the dawn, and ten nights﴾: the ten of al-Adha."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the even and the odd, and the night when it passes, is there in that an oath﴾:

The people of ta'wil differed about what is meant by the odd in His saying ﴿and the odd﴾. Some said: the even is the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), and the odd is the day of 'Arafah.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy, 'Abd al-Wahhab and Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from 'Awf, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The odd is the day of 'Arafah, and the even is the day of slaughter."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Awf informed us, saying: Zurarah ibn Awfa related to us, saying: Ibn Abbas said: "The even: the day of sacrifice; and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, who said: 'Ikrimah said, from Ibn Abbas: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- He related it to us again another time, and said: "The even: the days of sacrifice," and the rest of the narration is like it.
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿the even﴾: "The day of sacrifice"; ﴿and the odd﴾: "The day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from 'Ikrimah, who said: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- He said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Sinan, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿and ten nights and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "God swore by them because of what He knows of their virtue over the other days; and the better of these two days, because of what is known of their virtue over the other nights ﴿and the even and the odd﴾." He said: "The even: the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "'Ikrimah used to say: The even: the day of al-Adha, and the odd: the day of 'Arafah."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: 'Ikrimah said: "'Arafah is odd, and the sacrifice is even; 'Arafah is the ninth day, and the sacrifice is the tenth day."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿the even﴾: "The day of sacrifice," ﴿and the odd﴾: "The day of 'Arafah."

Others said: the even is the two days after the day of sacrifice, and the odd is the third day.

Those who said that:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: "The even: two days after the day of sacrifice, and the odd: the day of the final departure (al-nafr al-akhir)," as God says: ﴿Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾.

Others said: the even is all creation, and the odd is God.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: "God is the odd, and you are the even." It is also said: "The even: the dawn prayer, and the odd: the sunset prayer (maghrib)."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "Every creature of God is even: the heaven and the earth, the land and the sea, the jinn and mankind, the sun and the moon; and God alone is the odd."
- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Mujahid said regarding His saying ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾: "Disbelief and faith, happiness and misery, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, jinn and mankind; and the odd is God." He said: "And he said regarding the even and the odd the same."
- 'Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid related to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "God created pairs of everything, and God is the one odd, the eternal (samad)."
- Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "The even: the pair; and the odd: God."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "The odd is God, and whatever God created of things is even."

Others said: it refers to creation, because all creation is even and odd.

- He said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "All creation is even and odd, and He swore by creation."
- He said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said regarding that: "All creation is even." ﴿and the even and the odd﴾. He said: "My father used to say: everything God created is even and odd, so He swore by what He created, and He swore by what you see and what you do not see."

Others said: rather, it refers to the obligatory prayers, of which some are even, such as the dawn and noon prayers, and some are odd, such as the sunset prayer.

Those who said that:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "'Imran ibn Husayn used to say: ﴿the even and the odd﴾: the prayer."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: "'Imran said: they are the obligatory prayers, in which there is the even and the odd."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding ﴿and the even and the odd﴾: he said: "That is the sunset prayer. The even: two rak'ahs, and the odd: the third rak'ah." And some of them traced the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn to the Prophet.

Those who said that:

- Nasr ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: my father related to me, saying: Khalid ibn Qays related to me, from Qatadah, from 'Imran ibn 'Isam, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the even and the odd, that he said: "It is the prayer: of it is the even, and of it is the odd."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, that he was asked about the even and the odd, and he said: "'Imran ibn 'Isam al-Dab'i informed me, from a shaykh from the people of Basra, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: ﴿the even and the odd﴾: 'It is the prayer: of it is the even, and of it is the odd.'"
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Hammam ibn Yahya informed us, from 'Imran ibn 'Isam, from a shaykh from the people of Basra, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said regarding this verse ﴿the even and the odd﴾: "It is the prayer: of it is the even, and of it is the odd."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿the even and the odd﴾: "Indeed, of the prayer there is an even, and indeed of it there is an odd."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, that he was asked about the even and the odd, and he said: "al-Hasan said: it is the number." A report from the Prophet (ﷺ) supporting the view we mentioned from Abu al-Zubayr has also been transmitted.

Those who said that:

- 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani related to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab related to us, saying: 'Ayyash ibn 'Uqbah informed me, saying: Jubayr ibn Nu'aym related to me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The even: the two days; and the odd: the one day."

The correct view on this matter is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, swore by the even and the odd, and He did not specify one type of even or odd over another by any report or by reason. Every even and every odd is among what He swore by, according to what the people of ta'wil said, that it is included in His oath because of the generality of His swearing by it.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying ﴿and the odd (al-witr)﴾. The majority of reciters of Medina, Mecca and Basra, and some reciters of Kufa, read it with a kasra on the waw (al-witr).

The correct view on this matter is that both are well-known, widely transmitted recitations among the reciters of the regions, and two well-known dialects among the Arabs, so whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾:

He says: "and the night when it moves on and departs." From this one says: "So-and-so traveled by night (sara fulan laylan yasri)" when he traveled.

Some said: what is meant by His saying ﴿and the night when it passes﴾ is the night of Jam' (Muzdalifah), which is the night of Muzdalifah.

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we said in this.

Those who said that:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Qays informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, regarding ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: "until it takes away some of it from the rest."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he says: "when it departs."
- Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿and the night when it passes﴾: he said: "when it travels."
