Others said: rather, the meaning is: possessors of the pillars, the like of whom was not created in the lands. The like of the pillars was not created in the lands. They said: ﴿the like of whom was not created﴾ is a description of ﴿dhāt al-ʿimād﴾, and the hāʾ in "mithlahā" is from the mention of ﴿dhāt al-ʿimād﴾.

Mention of those who said this:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: and he mentioned something similar. This is a statement with no basis, because ʿimād is a masculine singular noun, and "allatī" is for the feminine, and the masculine is not described with "allatī". If that were a description of ʿimād, it would have been said "alladhī lam yukhlaq mithluhu fi al-bilād". And if you make "allatī" refer to Iram, and make the hāʾ in His words ﴿mithlahā﴾ refer back to it, and say: it is Damascus or Alexandria, then the lands of ʿĀd are those which God described in His Book, saying: ﴿And mention the brother of ʿĀd, when he warned his people in al-Aḥqāf﴾. Al-Aḥqāf is the plural of ḥiqf, which is what has bent and curved of sand; and neither Alexandria nor Damascus is among the lands of sand. Rather, that is al-Shiḥr in the lands of Ḥaḍramawt and what is adjacent to it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Thamūd, who hewed the rock in the valley﴾

He says: and to Thamūd, who cut through the rock and entered it and made it into houses, as He, may His praise be great, said: ﴿And they used to hew houses from the mountains, secure﴾. The Arabs say: "Fulān jāba al-falāt yajūbuhā jawban" when he entered it and crossed it. From this is the saying of Nābigha:

"Abū Laylā came to you, traversing with it the darkness,
the darkness of the night, traversing the wastelands, of wide reach."[[In the printed edition: "lam yumiʿin al-naẓar," they changed it, as they did in p. 55, note 3.]]

By His words "yajūb", he means: enters and crosses.

The people of ta'wil stated something similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

* ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words ﴿And Thamūd, who hewed the rock in the valley﴾, he said: meaning they split it.

* Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿And Thamūd, who hewed the rock in the valley﴾, meaning: Thamūd, the people of Ṣāliḥ, who used to hew houses out of the mountains.

* Muḥammad ibn ʿUmāra narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Yaḥyā, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿who hewed the rock in the valley﴾, he said: they hewed the mountains and made them into houses.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, concerning His words ﴿And Thamūd, who hewed the rock in the valley﴾: they hewed and carved them into houses.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: ﴿hewed the rock﴾: they bored through the rock.

* I was told by al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words ﴿hewed the rock in the valley﴾: he says: they cut the stones.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words ﴿who hewed the rock in the valley﴾: they struck houses and dwellings into the rock in the mountains, until they made dwellings in them. "Jābū": they hollowed out (jawwabū) the houses in the mountains. A speaker said:

"Surely everything other than God is perishing,
as a tribe of Shanīq and Māridd perished.
They struck, in every high rock-face (ṣalāʾa ṣaʿda),
with strong hands, sinewy forearms."[[In the Lisān (Miṣr), attributed to Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt. Ibn Barrī corrected it and attributed it to ʿAdī ibn Zayd. al-Miṣr: the barrier and boundary between two things. He says: he made the sun a boundary and sign between the night and the day.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾

He, His praise be great, says: Did you not see how your Lord also dealt with Pharaoh, the possessor of the stakes?

The people of ta'wil differed over the meaning of His words ﴿dhī al-awtād﴾, and why he was called that. Some said: its meaning is: possessor of the soldiers who strengthened his command, and they said: the stakes in this place are the soldiers.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾, he said: the stakes are the soldiers who made his command firm. It is said: Pharaoh used to drive iron stakes into their hands and feet, hanging them by them.

Others said: rather, he was called that because he used to stake people with stakes.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿dhī al-awtād﴾, he said: he used to stake people with stakes.

Others said: they were shaded pavilions and playgrounds under which he would play, made of stakes and ropes.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾: it was mentioned to us that they were shaded pavilions and playgrounds under which he would play, of stakes and ropes.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, ﴿dhī al-awtād﴾, he said: the one of the building; there were pavilions under which he would play, and stakes driven for him.

* He said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from Abū Rāfiʿ, who said: Pharaoh staked four stakes for his wife, then placed on her back a great millstone until she died.

Others said: rather, that was because he used to torment people with stakes.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ismāʿīl, from Maḥmūd, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾, he said: He used to place a man here and a man there, and a hand here and a hand there, with stakes.

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿dhī al-awtād﴾, he said: he used to stake people with stakes.

Others said: that was only because he had a building in which he tormented people.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ismāʿīl, from a man, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾, he said: he had minarets upon which he tormented them.

The statement most correct in my view is the statement of the one who said: what is meant is the stakes that are driven in, whether of wood or iron, because that is the well-known meaning of "awtād" (stakes). He was described by it either because he used to torment people with them, as Abū Rāfiʿ and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, or because he was played with by means of them.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Who transgressed in the lands﴾

By His words, His praise be great, ﴿alladhīn﴾ ("those who") He means: ʿĀd, Thamūd, Pharaoh and his army. By His words ﴿ṭaghaw﴾ ("transgressed") He means: they exceeded what their Lord had permitted for them, and rebelled against their Lord into what He forbade them, namely disbelief in Him.

* *

As for His words: ﴿in the lands﴾

: in which they were.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd, (6) Iram of the pillars, (7) the like of whom was not created in the lands, (8) and Thamūd, who hewed the rocks in the valley, (9) and Pharaoh, lord of the stakes, (10) who transgressed in the lands (11)﴾

.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd Iram﴾

He, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Did you not look, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart, and see how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd?

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed over the interpretation of His words ﴿Iram﴾. Some said: it is the name of a city. Then those who said this differed over which city was meant. Some of them said: it is Alexandria.

Mention of those who said this:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yaʿqub ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Zuhrī narrated to me, from Abū Ṣakhr, from al-Qurazī, that he heard him say: ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾ is Alexandria.

Abū Jaʿfar said: Others said: it is Damascus.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Hilālī, from the people of Basra, narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Majīd narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from al-Maqburī, concerning ﴿ʿĀd Iram of the pillars﴾: he said, Damascus.

Others said: by His words ﴿Iram﴾ is meant: a people (umma).

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn ʿUmāra narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Yaḥyā, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿Iram﴾, he said: a people.

Others said: the meaning of that is: the ancient (al-qadīma).

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿Iram﴾, he said: the ancient.

Others said: that is a tribe of ʿĀd.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, concerning His words: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd Iram of the pillars﴾, he said: We used to relate that Iram is a tribe of ʿĀd, the house of the kingdom of ʿĀd.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, concerning His words ﴿Iram﴾, he said: a tribe of ʿĀd, who were called Iram, the grandfather of ʿĀd.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd Iram﴾: God says: ʿĀd Iram, that is, ʿĀd son of Iram son of ʿAwṣ son of Sām son of Noah.

Others said: ﴿Iram﴾ means: the destroyed (al-hālik).

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd Iram﴾, meaning by Iram: the destroyed. Do you not see that you say: "The sons of so-and-so were destroyed" (aramma)?

* I was told by al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words ﴿ʿĀd Iram﴾: the destruction. Do you not see that you say: "The sons of so-and-so were destroyed (urima)", that is, they perished?[[His Dīwān 1:71.]]

The correct statement on this matter is that it is said: Iram is either a city in which ʿĀd used to dwell, and for that reason it was made to follow ʿĀd by way of attribution (ittibāʿ), and so it was not declined (lam yajrē); or it is the name of a tribe, and so it is also not declined, just as the names of tribes are not declined, such as Tamīm and Bakr and the like, when they are intended as tribes. As for the name ʿĀd, it is not declined because it is a non-Arabic name (aʿjamī).

As for what was reported from Mujāhid, that he said the meaning is "the ancient", this is a statement without meaning, because if that were its meaning it would be marked with tanwīn (nunation), and the absence of declension is evidence that it is not a qualifier or an attribute.

The most likely of the statements regarding it, in my view, is that it is the name of a tribe of ʿĀd. That is why the recitation came with the omission of the annexation of ʿĀd to it and the omission of its declension, just as one says: "Have you not considered what your Lord did to Tamīm Nahshal?" so Nahshal is not declined, though it is a tribe, and its non-declension is for that reason; and it is in the genitive position by way of attribution to Tamīm. If Iram were the name of a city, or the name of the grandfather of ʿĀd, the recitation would have come with ʿĀd annexed to it, as one says: "This is ʿAmr of Zabīd, and Ḥātim of Ṭayy, and Aʿshā of Hamdān." But in my opinion it is the name of a tribe among them, as Qatāda said, and God knows best. For this reason the readers (qurrāʾ) unanimously agreed on omitting the annexation and omitting the declension.

* *

As for His words: ﴿of the pillars﴾

The people of ta'wil differed over the meaning of His words ﴿dhāt al-ʿimād﴾ in this place, and why it was said of them. Some said: its meaning is: possessors of height, and they relied on the saying of the Arabs about a tall man: "a man muʿammad", and they said: they were people of tall bodies.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, ﴿of the pillars﴾: meaning, their height was like a pillar.

* Muḥammad ibn ʿUmāra narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Yaḥyā, from Mujāhid concerning His words ﴿of the pillars﴾, he said: they had a body reaching to the sky.

Others said: they were called ﴿of the pillars﴾ because they were a people of pillars (ʿamad), who sought the rain-clouds and moved to pasture wherever it was, then returned to their dwellings.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿al-ʿimād﴾, he said: a people of a pillar (ʿamūd), who did not stay in one place.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, ﴿of the pillars﴾, he said: It was mentioned to us that they were a people of a pillar, who did not settle, nomadic.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, ﴿of the pillars﴾, he said: they were a people of a pillar.

Others said: they were called that because of a building that one of them built, whose pillars he strengthened and whose structure he raised.

Mention of those who said this:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾: ʿĀd, the people of Hūd, built it and made it when they were in al-Aḥqāf. He said: ﴿the like of whom was not created﴾, like those constructions in the lands. He said: And likewise in al-Aḥqāf in Ḥaḍramawt, then ʿĀd was there. He said: And there are the sand dunes (aḥqāf al-raml), as God said: "in al-Aḥqāf of the sand", sands like mountains, which are shadowed and hollowed.

Others said: they were called that because of the strength of their bodies and their power.

Mention of those who said this:

* I was told by al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words ﴿of the pillars﴾: meaning, the severity and strength.

The statement most akin to what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates is the statement of the one who said: what is meant is that they were a people of a pillar, nomadic, because the known meaning of "ʿimād" in the speech of the Arabs is what tents are set up with, of wood and posts on which a structure is carried; and no building of theirs with pillars is known from a sound report. Rather, the people of ta'wil directed His words ﴿dhāt al-ʿimād﴾ to the meaning that it means the height of their bodies, while others directed it to the pillars of their tents. As for the pillars of buildings, none of the people of ta'wil, or few of them, directed it to that. The interpretation of the Qur'an is only directed to the most prevalent and well-known of its meanings, insofar as a way to that is found, rather than the most unusual.

* He said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from Abū Rāfiʿ, who said: Pharaoh staked four stakes for his wife, then placed on her back a great millstone until she died.

Others said: rather, that was because he used to torment people with stakes.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ismāʿīl, from Maḥmūd, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾, he said: He used to place a man here and a man there, and a hand here and a hand there, with stakes.

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿dhī al-awtād﴾, he said: he used to stake people with stakes.

Others said: that was only because he had a building in which he tormented people.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ismāʿīl, from a man, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾, he said: he had minarets upon which he tormented them.

The statement most correct in my view is the statement of the one who said: what is meant is the stakes that are driven in, whether of wood or iron, because that is the well-known meaning of "awtād" (stakes). He was described by it either because he used to torment people with them, as Abū Rāfiʿ and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, or because he was played with by means of them.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Who transgressed in the lands﴾

By His words, His praise be great, ﴿alladhīn﴾ ("those who") He means: ʿĀd, Thamūd, Pharaoh and his army. By His words ﴿ṭaghaw﴾ ("transgressed") He means: they exceeded what their Lord had permitted for them, and rebelled against their Lord into what He forbade them, namely disbelief in Him.

* *

As for His words: ﴿in the lands﴾

: in which they were.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd, (6) Iram of the pillars, (7) the like of whom was not created in the lands, (8) and Thamūd, who hewed the rocks in the valley, (9) and Pharaoh, lord of the stakes, (10) who transgressed in the lands (11)﴾

.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd Iram﴾

He, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Did you not look, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart, and see how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd?

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed over the interpretation of His words ﴿Iram﴾. Some said: it is the name of a city. Then those who said this differed over which city was meant. Some of them said: it is Alexandria.

Mention of those who said this:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yaʿqub ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Zuhrī narrated to me, from Abū Ṣakhr, from al-Qurazī, that he heard him say: ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾ is Alexandria.

Abū Jaʿfar said: Others said: it is Damascus.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Hilālī, from the people of Basra, narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Majīd narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from al-Maqburī, concerning ﴿ʿĀd Iram of the pillars﴾: he said, Damascus.

Others said: by His words ﴿Iram﴾ is meant: a people (umma).

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn ʿUmāra narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Yaḥyā, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿Iram﴾, he said: a people.

Others said: the meaning of that is: the ancient (al-qadīma).

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿Iram﴾, he said: the ancient.

Others said: that is a tribe of ʿĀd.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, concerning His words: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd Iram of the pillars﴾, he said: We used to relate that Iram is a tribe of ʿĀd, the house of the kingdom of ʿĀd.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, concerning His words ﴿Iram﴾, he said: a tribe of ʿĀd, who were called Iram, the grandfather of ʿĀd.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd Iram﴾: God says: ʿĀd Iram, that is, ʿĀd son of Iram son of ʿAwṣ son of Sām son of Noah.

Others said: ﴿Iram﴾ means: the destroyed (al-hālik).

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd Iram﴾, meaning by Iram: the destroyed. Do you not see that you say: "The sons of so-and-so were destroyed" (aramma)?

* I was told by al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words ﴿ʿĀd Iram﴾: the destruction. Do you not see that you say: "The sons of so-and-so were destroyed (urima)", that is, they perished?[[His Dīwān 1:71.]]

The correct statement on this matter is that it is said: Iram is either a city in which ʿĀd used to dwell, and for that reason it was made to follow ʿĀd by way of attribution (ittibāʿ), and so it was not declined (lam yajrē); or it is the name of a tribe, and so it is also not declined, just as the names of tribes are not declined, such as Tamīm and Bakr and the like, when they are intended as tribes. As for the name ʿĀd, it is not declined because it is a non-Arabic name (aʿjamī).

As for what was reported from Mujāhid, that he said the meaning is "the ancient", this is a statement without meaning, because if that were its meaning it would be marked with tanwīn (nunation), and the absence of declension is evidence that it is not a qualifier or an attribute.

The most likely of the statements regarding it, in my view, is that it is the name of a tribe of ʿĀd. That is why the recitation came with the omission of the annexation of ʿĀd to it and the omission of its declension, just as one says: "Have you not considered what your Lord did to Tamīm Nahshal?" so Nahshal is not declined, though it is a tribe, and its non-declension is for that reason; and it is in the genitive position by way of attribution to Tamīm. If Iram were the name of a city, or the name of the grandfather of ʿĀd, the recitation would have come with ʿĀd annexed to it, as one says: "This is ʿAmr of Zabīd, and Ḥātim of Ṭayy, and Aʿshā of Hamdān." But in my opinion it is the name of a tribe among them, as Qatāda said, and God knows best. For this reason the readers (qurrāʾ) unanimously agreed on omitting the annexation and omitting the declension.

* *

As for His words: ﴿of the pillars﴾

The people of ta'wil differed over the meaning of His words ﴿dhāt al-ʿimād﴾ in this place, and why it was said of them. Some said: its meaning is: possessors of height, and they relied on the saying of the Arabs about a tall man: "a man muʿammad", and they said: they were people of tall bodies.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, ﴿of the pillars﴾: meaning, their height was like a pillar.

* Muḥammad ibn ʿUmāra narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Yaḥyā, from Mujāhid concerning His words ﴿of the pillars﴾, he said: they had a body reaching to the sky.

Others said: they were called ﴿of the pillars﴾ because they were a people of pillars (ʿamad), who sought the rain-clouds and moved to pasture wherever it was, then returned to their dwellings.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿al-ʿimād﴾, he said: a people of a pillar (ʿamūd), who did not stay in one place.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, ﴿of the pillars﴾, he said: It was mentioned to us that they were a people of a pillar, who did not settle, nomadic.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, ﴿of the pillars﴾, he said: they were a people of a pillar.

Others said: they were called that because of a building that one of them built, whose pillars he strengthened and whose structure he raised.

Mention of those who said this:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾: ʿĀd, the people of Hūd, built it and made it when they were in al-Aḥqāf. He said: ﴿the like of whom was not created﴾, like those constructions in the lands. He said: And likewise in al-Aḥqāf in Ḥaḍramawt, then ʿĀd was there. He said: And there are the sand dunes (aḥqāf al-raml), as God said: "in al-Aḥqāf of the sand", sands like mountains, which are shadowed and hollowed.

Others said: they were called that because of the strength of their bodies and their power.

Mention of those who said this:

* I was told by al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words ﴿of the pillars﴾: meaning, the severity and strength.

The statement most akin to what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates is the statement of the one who said: what is meant is that they were a people of a pillar, nomadic, because the known meaning of "ʿimād" in the speech of the Arabs is what tents are set up with, of wood and posts on which a structure is carried; and no building of theirs with pillars is known from a sound report. Rather, the people of ta'wil directed His words ﴿dhāt al-ʿimād﴾ to the meaning that it means the height of their bodies, while others directed it to the pillars of their tents. As for the pillars of buildings, none of the people of ta'wil, or few of them, directed it to that. The interpretation of the Qur'an is only directed to the most prevalent and well-known of its meanings, insofar as a way to that is found, rather than the most unusual.

* *

As for His words: ﴿the like of whom was not created in the lands﴾

He, His praise be great, says: Did you not see how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd, Iram, the like of whom was not created in the lands, meaning: the like of ʿĀd. The pronoun (hāʾ) refers back to ʿĀd. It is also permissible that it refers back to Iram, as we have already explained, that it is a tribe. What is meant by His words "was not created" is in size, might and strength.

The people of ta'wil stated something similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, concerning His words ﴿the like of whom was not created in the lands﴾: it was mentioned that they were twelve cubits tall in the sky.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: possessors of the pillars, the like of whom was not created in the lands. The like of the pillars was not created in the lands. They said: ﴿the like of whom was not created﴾ is a description of ﴿dhāt al-ʿimād﴾, and the hāʾ in "mithlahā" is from the mention of ﴿dhāt al-ʿimād﴾.

Mention of those who said this:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: and he mentioned something similar. This is a statement with no basis, because ʿimād is a masculine singular noun, and "allatī" is for the feminine, and the masculine is not described with "allatī". If that were a description of ʿimād, it would have been said "alladhī lam yukhlaq mithluhu fi al-bilād". And if you make "allatī" refer to Iram, and make the hāʾ in His words ﴿mithlahā﴾ refer back to it, and say: it is Damascus or Alexandria, then the lands of ʿĀd are those which God described in His Book, saying: ﴿And mention the brother of ʿĀd, when he warned his people in al-Aḥqāf﴾. Al-Aḥqāf is the plural of ḥiqf, which is what has bent and curved of sand; and neither Alexandria nor Damascus is among the lands of sand. Rather, that is al-Shiḥr in the lands of Ḥaḍramawt and what is adjacent to it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Thamūd, who hewed the rock in the valley﴾

He says: and to Thamūd, who cut through the rock and entered it and made it into houses, as He, may His praise be great, said: ﴿And they used to hew houses from the mountains, secure﴾. The Arabs say: "Fulān jāba al-falāt yajūbuhā jawban" when he entered it and crossed it. From this is the saying of Nābigha:

"Abū Laylā came to you, traversing with it the darkness,
the darkness of the night, traversing the wastelands, of wide reach."[[In the printed edition: "lam yumiʿin al-naẓar," they changed it, as they did in p. 55, note 3.]]

By His words "yajūb", he means: enters and crosses.

The people of ta'wil stated something similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

* ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words ﴿And Thamūd, who hewed the rock in the valley﴾, he said: meaning they split it.

* Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿And Thamūd, who hewed the rock in the valley﴾, meaning: Thamūd, the people of Ṣāliḥ, who used to hew houses out of the mountains.

* Muḥammad ibn ʿUmāra narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Yaḥyā, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿who hewed the rock in the valley﴾, he said: they hewed the mountains and made them into houses.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, concerning His words ﴿And Thamūd, who hewed the rock in the valley﴾: they hewed and carved them into houses.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, who said: ﴿hewed the rock﴾: they bored through the rock.

* I was told by al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words ﴿hewed the rock in the valley﴾: he says: they cut the stones.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words ﴿who hewed the rock in the valley﴾: they struck houses and dwellings into the rock in the mountains, until they made dwellings in them. "Jābū": they hollowed out (jawwabū) the houses in the mountains. A speaker said:

"Surely everything other than God is perishing,
as a tribe of Shanīq and Māridd perished.
They struck, in every high rock-face (ṣalāʾa ṣaʿda),
with strong hands, sinewy forearms."[[In the Lisān (Miṣr), attributed to Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt. Ibn Barrī corrected it and attributed it to ʿAdī ibn Zayd. al-Miṣr: the barrier and boundary between two things. He says: he made the sun a boundary and sign between the night and the day.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾

He, His praise be great, says: Did you not see how your Lord also dealt with Pharaoh, the possessor of the stakes?

The people of ta'wil differed over the meaning of His words ﴿dhī al-awtād﴾, and why he was called that. Some said: its meaning is: possessor of the soldiers who strengthened his command, and they said: the stakes in this place are the soldiers.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾, he said: the stakes are the soldiers who made his command firm. It is said: Pharaoh used to drive iron stakes into their hands and feet, hanging them by them.

Others said: rather, he was called that because he used to stake people with stakes.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿dhī al-awtād﴾, he said: he used to stake people with stakes.

Others said: they were shaded pavilions and playgrounds under which he would play, made of stakes and ropes.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾: it was mentioned to us that they were shaded pavilions and playgrounds under which he would play, of stakes and ropes.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, ﴿dhī al-awtād﴾, he said: the one of the building; there were pavilions under which he would play, and stakes driven for him.

* He said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from Abū Rāfiʿ, who said: Pharaoh staked four stakes for his wife, then placed on her back a great millstone until she died.

Others said: rather, that was because he used to torment people with stakes.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ismāʿīl, from Maḥmūd, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾, he said: He used to place a man here and a man there, and a hand here and a hand there, with stakes.

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words ﴿dhī al-awtād﴾, he said: he used to stake people with stakes.

Others said: that was only because he had a building in which he tormented people.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ismāʿīl, from a man, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾, he said: he had minarets upon which he tormented them.

The statement most correct in my view is the statement of the one who said: what is meant is the stakes that are driven in, whether of wood or iron, because that is the well-known meaning of "awtād" (stakes). He was described by it either because he used to torment people with them, as Abū Rāfiʿ and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, or because he was played with by means of them.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Who transgressed in the lands﴾

By His words, His praise be great, ﴿alladhīn﴾ ("those who") He means: ʿĀd, Thamūd, Pharaoh and his army. By His words ﴿ṭaghaw﴾ ("transgressed") He means: they exceeded what their Lord had permitted for them, and rebelled against their Lord into what He forbade them, namely disbelief in Him.

* *

As for His words: ﴿in the lands﴾

: in which they were.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 89, verses 12–15:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So they multiplied corruption therein. Then your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment. Indeed, your Lord is ever in observation.﴾ ﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him and honours him and gives him favours, he says, "My Lord has honoured me."﴾

His saying, the Exalted, means: they multiplied sins in the lands and committed what Allah had forbidden them. ﴿Then your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment﴾ means: your Lord, O Muhammad, sent down His punishment upon them and brought down His vengeance upon them, because they spread corruption in the lands and transgressed against Allah therein. It was also said: "Then your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment." The retributions that descended upon them were, either a wind that destroyed them, or a violent quake that crushed them, or a drowning that destroyed them, without being struck with a whip or a staff. This is because the most painful punishment among the people to whom this Qur'an was addressed was flogging with whips. So the people frequently used to describe the severity of the punishment with which a man among them was tormented by saying, "So-and-so was beaten with whips," until this became a proverb, and they used it for everyone tormented with some kind of severe punishment, saying: "A scourge of punishment was poured upon him."

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿a scourge of punishment﴾ he said: "That with which they were punished."

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Then your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment﴾: "The punishment with which He punished them, He named it a scourge of punishment."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever in observation﴾

His saying, the Exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ means: Indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, for these people whose stories I have related to you, and for their like among the people of disbelief, is ever in observation, watching their deeds in this world and in the Hereafter, at the bridges of Hell, to hurl them into it when they arrive on the Day of Resurrection.

The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: the meaning of His saying ﴿in observation﴾ is that He sees and hears.

Mention of those who said that:

'Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever in observation﴾, he said: "He sees and hears."

Others said: it means that He is in a place of watching over the people of injustice.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from al-Mubarak ibn Mujahid, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding this verse, he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the Lord will command His Throne, and it will be placed over the Fire, and He will settle upon it, then He will say: "By My might and My majesty, no one bearing an injustice shall pass beyond Me today." This is His saying: ﴿in observation﴾.

He said: al-Hakam ibn Bashir related to us, he said: 'Amr ibn Qays related to us, he said: It reached me that over Hell there are three bridges: a bridge upon which is trust (amanah), when they pass over it, it says: "O Lord, this one is trustworthy; O Lord, this one is a traitor." And a bridge upon which are the ties of kinship, when they pass over it, it says: "O Lord, this one maintained ties; O Lord, this one severed them." And a bridge upon which is the Lord: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever in observation﴾.

He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever in observation﴾, meaning: Hell has three bridges: a bridge upon which is mercy, a bridge upon which is trust, and a bridge upon which is the Lord, blessed and exalted.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever in observation﴾, he said: "An observatory for the deeds of the children of Adam."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him﴾

The interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿But as for man, when his Lord tries him and honors him and bestows favor upon him, he says, "My Lord has honored me." * *

His saying: ﴿But as for man, when his Lord tries him, and provides for him, so He straitens his provision for him﴾

He says: as for man, when his Lord tests him with poverty, ﴿so He straitens his provision for him﴾, meaning: He restricts his provision and reduces it, so that his wealth does not increase and He does not widen it for him. ﴿Then he says, "My Lord has humiliated me"﴾, meaning: that person says, "My Lord has humiliated me," i.e., has abased me with poverty, and he does not thank God for the soundness of his limbs that He granted him and the well-being of his body that He provided him.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿But as for man, when his Lord tries him, and so He straitens his provision for him, then he says, "My Lord has humiliated me"﴾: How quickly the son of Adam disbelieves.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿so He straitens his provision for him﴾: He said: He restricted it.

The reciters differed in the reading of His saying ﴿fa-qadara ʿalayhi rizqahu﴾. The majority of the reciters of the regional centers read it with the light form, ﴿faqadara﴾, meaning "faqatara" (he restricted). The exception was Abu Ja'far the reciter, who read it with the intensive form ﴿faqaddara﴾. It is reported from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' that he used to say: qaddara, meaning He gives him what suffices him, and he would say: if He did that to him, he would not say, "My Lord has humiliated me."

The correct reading in our view is the light form, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it.

* *

His saying: ﴿No! Rather, you do not honor the orphan﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning what is meant by His saying ﴿No!﴾ in this place, and what He was rejecting by it. Some of them said: the Exalted rejected that the cause of one's honor is the abundance of one's wealth, and the cause of one's humiliation is the scarcity of one's wealth.

Those who said this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿But as for man, when his Lord tries him, and so He straitens his provision for him, then he says, "My Lord has humiliated me"﴾: How quickly the son of Adam disbelieves. God, the Exalted, says: "No! Indeed I do not honor whoever I honor with the abundance of the world, nor do I humiliate whoever I humiliate with its scarcity; rather, I honor whoever I honor with My obedience, and I humiliate whoever I humiliate with My disobedience."

Others said: rather, the Exalted rejected man's praise of his Lord for His blessings but not for his poverty, and his complaint of need. They said: the meaning of the speech is, "No!", i.e., it should not have been so; rather, he should have praised Him for both conditions, for wealth and for poverty.

The more correct of these two views is the view reported from Qatadah, because of the indication of His saying ﴿Rather, you do not honor the orphan﴾ and the verses that follow, showing that He humiliated those who were humiliated only because they do not honor the orphan, do not urge the feeding of the poor, and the other matters He enumerated. In His clarifying the cause for which He humiliated those He humiliated, there is clear evidence of the cause of His honoring those He honored. And in His clarifying this right after His saying ﴿But as for man, when his Lord tries him and honors him and bestows favor upon him, he says, "My Lord has honored me." But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me"﴾ is a clear explanation of what he rejected in his saying, as we have described.

* *

His saying: ﴿Rather, you do not honor the orphan﴾

The Exalted says: Rather, I have humiliated those whom I humiliated because they do not honor the orphan. He turned the speech into address, saying: Rather, you do not honor the orphan, and therefore I have humiliated you. ﴿and you do not urge one another to feed the poor﴾.

The reciters differed in the reading of this. The people of Medina, Abu Ja'far, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa read ﴿la tukrimūna al-yatīm wa-la tahāddūna﴾ with the taʾ (second person) also, with its fatḥah and with the alif affirmed, meaning: and none of you urges another to feed the poor. Some reciters of Mecca and the majority of reciters of Medina read it with the taʾ and its fatḥah and without the alif, ﴿wa-la tahuddūna﴾, meaning: and you do not command the feeding of the poor. The majority of the reciters of Basra read ﴿yahuddūna﴾ with the yāʾ (third person) and without the alif, meaning: those who say, when their Lord tries them and honors them and bestows favor, "My Lord has honored me," and when He restricts their provision, "My Lord has humiliated me," do not honor the orphan, and do not urge one another to feed the poor. Likewise, the Basran reciters mentioned read ﴿yukrimūna﴾ and all the other verbs with it with the yāʾ, as a report about those I mentioned. It is also reported of some of them that he read ﴿tuhāḍḍūna﴾ with the taʾ, its ḍammah, and the affirmed alif, meaning: and you do not guard (one another's obligations).

My view on the correct statement regarding this is that these are well-known readings among the reciters of the regional centers; I mean, the three readings are all sound in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

* *

His saying: ﴿And you devour inheritance, devouring greedily﴾

The Exalted says: And you, O people, devour the inheritance, devouring greedily, meaning: devouring intensely, leaving nothing of it, from the saying: "I licked (lamma) what was on the table entirely," so I lick it (alammuhu) lamman, when I eat what is on it and reach all of it.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

⁕ ʿAmr ibn Saʿid ibn Yasar al-Qurashi narrated to me, saying: al-Ansari narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿And you devour inheritance, devouring greedily﴾: He said: the inheritance.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And you devour inheritance﴾: that is, the inheritance; and likewise in His saying ﴿devouring greedily﴾.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And you devour inheritance, devouring greedily﴾: He says: you eat greedily, intensely.

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿And you devour inheritance, devouring greedily﴾: He said: his share and the share of his companion.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿devouring greedily﴾: He said: al-Lamm is al-saff, gathering up everything.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding ﴿devouring greedily﴾: that is, intensely.

⁕ I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿devouring greedily﴾: he says: intense eating.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding God's saying ﴿And you devour inheritance, devouring greedily﴾: He said: the greedy eater (al-lamm) is one who eats everything he finds without asking, so he eats what is his and what belongs to his companion. They did not give inheritance to women, nor to the young children. He recited: ﴿They ask you concerning women. Say, "God gives you a ruling concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan girls to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them, and whom you desire to marry, and the oppressed among the children"﴾ — meaning: you do not give them inheritance either — ﴿devouring greedily﴾: he eats his inheritance, and everything about which he does not ask and does not know whether it is lawful or unlawful.

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And you devour inheritance, devouring greedily﴾: He says: safan (greedy consumption).

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah al-Tinnisi narrated to us, from Zuhayr, from Salim, who said: I heard Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah say regarding this verse ﴿And you devour inheritance, devouring greedily﴾: al-lamm is transgression in inheritance: one eats his own inheritance and the inheritance of others.

And His saying: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: And when your Lord comes, O Muhammad, and His angels in rows, rank after rank.

As follows:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, both said: Awf narrated to us, from Abu al-Minhal, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be stretched like a hide, and its breadth will be increased by such and such, and all creation will be gathered on one plain, jinn and humankind. Then, when that day comes, this lowest heaven will be emptied of its inhabitants onto the surface of the earth, and the inhabitants of the heavens alone are more than the inhabitants of the earth, jinn and humankind, by twice over. When they are scattered over the surface of the earth, they are terrified of them, and they say: "Is our Lord among you?" They are frightened by their words and say: "Glory to our Lord, He is not among us, and He is coming." Then the second heaven is emptied, and the inhabitants of the second heaven alone are more than the inhabitants of the lowest heaven and all the inhabitants of the earth by twice over, jinn and humankind. When they are scattered over the surface of the earth, the inhabitants of the earth come to them in fear and say: "Is our Lord among you?" They are frightened by their words and say: "Glory to our Lord, He is not among us, and He is coming." Then the heavens are emptied heaven by heaven; each time a heaven is emptied of its inhabitants, they are more than the inhabitants of the heavens beneath it and all the inhabitants of the earth by twice over. When they are scattered over the surface of the earth, the inhabitants of the earth come to them in fear, and they say to them the same, and they return to them the same, until the seventh heaven is emptied, and the inhabitants of the seventh heaven are more than the inhabitants of six heavens and all the inhabitants of the earth by twice over. Then God comes among them, and the nations are kneeling in rows, and a caller calls: "You will know today who are the people of nobility; let those who praise God stand in every state." He said: They stand and proceed to Paradise. Then he calls a second time: "You will know today who are the people of nobility: where are those whose sides shun their beds, who call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and spend from what We have provided them?" And they proceed to Paradise. Then he calls a third time: "You will know today who are the people of nobility: where are those whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God, and the establishment of prayer and giving of zakat, who fear a Day when hearts and eyes will be turned about?" They stand and proceed to Paradise. When three of these have been taken, a neck (ʿunuq) comes forth from the Fire, overlooks the creation, has two eyes that see and an eloquent tongue, and says: "I have been assigned to take from you three: every stubborn tyrant," and it snatches them from the rows as a bird snatches sesame seeds, and they are confined in Hell. Then it comes out a second time and says: "I have been assigned to take from you those who harmed God and His Messenger," and it snatches them as a bird snatches sesame seeds, and they are confined in Hell. Then it comes out a third time. Awf said: Abu al-Minhal said: I think it says: "I have been assigned to the people of images," and it snatches them from the rows as a bird snatches sesame seeds, and they are confined in Hell. When three of these and three of those have been taken, the scrolls are unrolled, the scales are set up, and the creation is summoned to reckoning.

- Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, he said: Abu Usama narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, he said: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God commands the lowest heaven with its inhabitants, and those in it of the angels descend and surround the earth and whoever is upon it. Then the second, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, then the seventh, and they line up, one row behind another. Then the Highest King descends upon its left flank, Hell. When the people of the earth see it, they flee, but they find no region of the earth except that they find seven rows of angels, so they return to the place where they were. This is the saying of God: ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the Day of Calling, the Day you will turn back in retreat; you will have no protector from God﴾, and this is His saying: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank, and Hell is brought forth that Day﴾, and His saying: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass; you will not pass except with authority﴾, and this is God's saying: ﴿And the sky will split open, for it that Day will be frail, and the angels will be upon its extremities﴾.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "You will be made to stand one standing on the Day of Resurrection for the length of seventy years; you will not be looked upon nor will judgment be passed between you. You will be confined, so you will weep until the tears stop, then you will shed blood, and you will weep until it reaches your chins, or it bridles you, and you will cry out. Then you will say: 'Who will intercede for us with our Lord, so that He may judge between us?' They will say: 'Who is more worthy of that than your father? God made his dust and his creation with His hand, breathed into him of His spirit, and spoke to him directly.' So Adam is approached and asked, but he refuses. Then they seek the prophets one after another, each time they come to a prophet, he refuses." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "until they come to me. When they come to me, I will go out until I come to al-Fahs." Abu Hurayra said: O Messenger of God, what is al-Fahs? He said: "In front of the Throne; I will fall in prostration, and I will not cease prostrating until God sends an angel to me, who takes me by the arm and raises me. Then God says to me: 'Muhammad,' and He knows best. I say: 'Yes.' He says: 'What is your matter?' I say: 'O my Lord, You promised me intercession; intercede for me regarding Your creation, and judge between them.' He says: 'I have interceded for you. I will come to you and judge between you.'" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Then I turn back until I stand with the people, and while we are standing, we hear an intense sound from the sky, which frightens us. The inhabitants of the lowest heaven descend, twice the number of those on earth of jinn and humankind, until when they approach the earth, the earth is lit by their light, and they take their ranks, and we say to them: 'Is our Lord among you?' They say: 'No, but He is coming.' Then the inhabitants of the second heaven descend, twice the number of the angels who descended, and twice the number of those in it of jinn and humankind, until when they approach the earth, the earth is lit by their light, and they take their ranks, and we say to them: 'Is our Lord among you?' They say: 'No, but He is coming.' Then the inhabitants of the heavens descend in proportion to that multiplication, until the Almighty descends in clouds of cloud and angels, and they have a murmur of their glorification, saying: 'Glory to the Possessor of dominion and sovereignty; glory to the Lord of the Throne, the Possessor of majesty; glory to the Living who does not die; glory to the One who causes the creatures to die and does not die; Most Holy, Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit; Holy, Holy; glory to our Exalted Lord; glory to the Possessor of majesty, sovereignty, grandeur, authority and greatness, glory to Him forever and ever.' On that day eight will carry His Throne, and today they are four; their feet are on the lowest limits of the earth, the heavens reach their waists, and the Throne is on their shoulders. God places His Throne wherever He wills on the earth. Then He calls out with a call that makes all creatures hear, saying: 'O assembly of jinn and humankind, I have been silent since the day I created you until this day of yours; I hear your speech and see your deeds, so listen to Me. These are your scrolls and your deeds being read to you. Whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame none but himself.' Then God commands Hell, and it brings forth from it a bright, dark neck. Then God says: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan, for he is to you a clear enemy?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿This is Hell which you were promised﴾, and ﴿Separate yourselves today, O criminals﴾, so people separate and fall to their knees, and this is what God means: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling; every nation will be called to its record today...﴾ the verse. Then God judges among His creatures, jinn, humankind and animals, for He will exact retribution on that day for the hornless sheep from the horned one, until no claim remains between one and another. Then God says: 'Be dust,' and at that the disbeliever says: 'Would that I were dust.' Then God, Glorified is He, judges between jinn and humankind."

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾: the rows of the angels.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And Hell is brought forth that Day﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: And God brings Hell forth that day.

As follows:

- Al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to us, he said: Marwan al-Fazari narrated to us, from al-Ala ibn Khalid al-Asadi, from Shaqiq ibn Salama, who said: Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said regarding His saying: ﴿And Hell is brought forth that Day﴾: It will be brought led by seventy thousand reins, with each rein seventy thousand angels leading it.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Asim ibn Bahdala, from Abu Wa'il: ﴿And Hell is brought forth that Day﴾: It will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, led by seventy thousand reins, with each rein seventy thousand angels.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, he said: Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: "Its two sides: Paradise and the Fire." He said: This is when He descends from His Throne to His Footstool for the reckoning of His creation, and he recited: ﴿And Hell is brought forth that Day﴾.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿And Hell is brought forth that Day﴾: It is brought bridled.

And His saying: ﴿On that Day man will remember﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: On that day man will remember his neglect in the world regarding obedience to God and what brings him closer to Him of righteous deeds. ﴿But how will the remembrance benefit him?﴾ meaning: by what means will remembrance be for him?

And the people of interpretation said according to what we have said on this matter.

And His saying: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: And when your Lord comes, O Muhammad, and His angels in rows, rank after rank.

As follows:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, both said: Awf narrated to us, from Abu al-Minhal, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be stretched like a hide, and its breadth will be increased by such and such, and all creation will be gathered on one plain, jinn and humankind. Then, when that day comes, this lowest heaven will be emptied of its inhabitants onto the surface of the earth, and the inhabitants of the heavens alone are more than the inhabitants of the earth, jinn and humankind, by twice over. When they are scattered over the surface of the earth, they are terrified of them, and they say: "Is our Lord among you?" They are frightened by their words and say: "Glory to our Lord, He is not among us, and He is coming." Then the second heaven is emptied, and the inhabitants of the second heaven alone are more than the inhabitants of the lowest heaven and all the inhabitants of the earth by twice over, jinn and humankind. When they are scattered over the surface of the earth, the inhabitants of the earth come to them in fear and say: "Is our Lord among you?" They are frightened by their words and say: "Glory to our Lord, He is not among us, and He is coming." Then the heavens are emptied heaven by heaven; each time a heaven is emptied of its inhabitants, they are more than the inhabitants of the heavens beneath it and all the inhabitants of the earth by twice over. When they are scattered over the surface of the earth, the inhabitants of the earth come to them in fear, and they say to them the same, and they return to them the same, until the seventh heaven is emptied, and the inhabitants of the seventh heaven are more than the inhabitants of six heavens and all the inhabitants of the earth by twice over. Then God comes among them, and the nations are kneeling in rows, and a caller calls: "You will know today who are the people of nobility; let those who praise God stand in every state." He said: They stand and proceed to Paradise. Then he calls a second time: "You will know today who are the people of nobility: where are those whose sides shun their beds, who call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and spend from what We have provided them?" And they proceed to Paradise. Then he calls a third time: "You will know today who are the people of nobility: where are those whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God, and the establishment of prayer and giving of zakat, who fear a Day when hearts and eyes will be turned about?" They stand and proceed to Paradise. When three of these have been taken, a neck (ʿunuq) comes forth from the Fire, overlooks the creation, has two eyes that see and an eloquent tongue, and says: "I have been assigned to take from you three: every stubborn tyrant," and it snatches them from the rows as a bird snatches sesame seeds, and they are confined in Hell. Then it comes out a second time and says: "I have been assigned to take from you those who harmed God and His Messenger," and it snatches them as a bird snatches sesame seeds, and they are confined in Hell. Then it comes out a third time. Awf said: Abu al-Minhal said: I think it says: "I have been assigned to the people of images," and it snatches them from the rows as a bird snatches sesame seeds, and they are confined in Hell. When three of these and three of those have been taken, the scrolls are unrolled, the scales are set up, and the creation is summoned to reckoning.

- Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, he said: Abu Usama narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, he said: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God commands the lowest heaven with its inhabitants, and those in it of the angels descend and surround the earth and whoever is upon it. Then the second, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, then the seventh, and they line up, one row behind another. Then the Highest King descends upon its left flank, Hell. When the people of the earth see it, they flee, but they find no region of the earth except that they find seven rows of angels, so they return to the place where they were. This is the saying of God: ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the Day of Calling, the Day you will turn back in retreat; you will have no protector from God﴾, and this is His saying: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank, and Hell is brought forth that Day﴾, and His saying: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass; you will not pass except with authority﴾, and this is God's saying: ﴿And the sky will split open, for it that Day will be frail, and the angels will be upon its extremities﴾.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "You will be made to stand one standing on the Day of Resurrection for the length of seventy years; you will not be looked upon nor will judgment be passed between you. You will be confined, so you will weep until the tears stop, then you will shed blood, and you will weep until it reaches your chins, or it bridles you, and you will cry out. Then you will say: 'Who will intercede for us with our Lord, so that He may judge between us?' They will say: 'Who is more worthy of that than your father? God made his dust and his creation with His hand, breathed into him of His spirit, and spoke to him directly.' So Adam is approached and asked, but he refuses. Then they seek the prophets one after another, each time they come to a prophet, he refuses." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "until they come to me. When they come to me, I will go out until I come to al-Fahs." Abu Hurayra said: O Messenger of God, what is al-Fahs? He said: "In front of the Throne; I will fall in prostration, and I will not cease prostrating until God sends an angel to me, who takes me by the arm and raises me. Then God says to me: 'Muhammad,' and He knows best. I say: 'Yes.' He says: 'What is your matter?' I say: 'O my Lord, You promised me intercession; intercede for me regarding Your creation, and judge between them.' He says: 'I have interceded for you. I will come to you and judge between you.'" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Then I turn back until I stand with the people, and while we are standing, we hear an intense sound from the sky, which frightens us. The inhabitants of the lowest heaven descend, twice the number of those on earth of jinn and humankind, until when they approach the earth, the earth is lit by their light, and they take their ranks, and we say to them: 'Is our Lord among you?' They say: 'No, but He is coming.' Then the inhabitants of the second heaven descend, twice the number of the angels who descended, and twice the number of those in it of jinn and humankind, until when they approach the earth, the earth is lit by their light, and they take their ranks, and we say to them: 'Is our Lord among you?' They say: 'No, but He is coming.' Then the inhabitants of the heavens descend in proportion to that multiplication, until the Almighty descends in clouds of cloud and angels, and they have a murmur of their glorification, saying: 'Glory to the Possessor of dominion and sovereignty; glory to the Lord of the Throne, the Possessor of majesty; glory to the Living who does not die; glory to the One who causes the creatures to die and does not die; Most Holy, Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit; Holy, Holy; glory to our Exalted Lord; glory to the Possessor of majesty, sovereignty, grandeur, authority and greatness, glory to Him forever and ever.' On that day eight will carry His Throne, and today they are four; their feet are on the lowest limits of the earth, the heavens reach their waists, and the Throne is on their shoulders. God places His Throne wherever He wills on the earth. Then He calls out with a call that makes all creatures hear, saying: 'O assembly of jinn and humankind, I have been silent since the day I created you until this day of yours; I hear your speech and see your deeds, so listen to Me. These are your scrolls and your deeds being read to you. Whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame none but himself.' Then God commands Hell, and it brings forth from it a bright, dark neck. Then God says: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan, for he is to you a clear enemy?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿This is Hell which you were promised﴾, and ﴿Separate yourselves today, O criminals﴾, so people separate and fall to their knees, and this is what God means: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling; every nation will be called to its record today...﴾ the verse. Then God judges among His creatures, jinn, humankind and animals, for He will exact retribution on that day for the hornless sheep from the horned one, until no claim remains between one and another. Then God says: 'Be dust,' and at that the disbeliever says: 'Would that I were dust.' Then God, Glorified is He, judges between jinn and humankind."
