Then the inhabitants of the second heaven descend, twice the number of the angels who descended, and twice the number of those in it of jinn and humankind, until when they approach the earth, the earth is lit by their light, and they take their ranks, and we say to them: 'Is our Lord among you?' They say: 'No, but He is coming.' Then the inhabitants of the heavens descend in proportion to that multiplication, until the Almighty descends in clouds of cloud and angels, and they have a murmur of their glorification, saying: 'Glory to the Possessor of dominion and sovereignty; glory to the Lord of the Throne, the Possessor of majesty; glory to the Living who does not die; glory to the One who causes the creatures to die and does not die; Most Holy, Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit; Holy, Holy; glory to our Exalted Lord; glory to the Possessor of majesty, sovereignty, grandeur, authority and greatness, glory to Him forever and ever.' On that day eight will carry His Throne, and today they are four; their feet are on the lowest limits of the earth, the heavens reach their waists, and the Throne is on their shoulders. God places His Throne wherever He wills on the earth. Then He calls out with a call that makes all creatures hear, saying: 'O assembly of jinn and humankind, I have been silent since the day I created you until this day of yours; I hear your speech and see your deeds, so listen to Me. These are your scrolls and your deeds being read to you. Whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame none but himself.' Then God commands Hell, and it brings forth from it a bright, dark neck. Then God says: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan, for he is to you a clear enemy?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿This is Hell which you were promised﴾, and ﴿Separate yourselves today, O criminals﴾, so people separate and fall to their knees, and this is what God means: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling; every nation will be called to its record today...﴾ the verse. Then God judges among His creatures, jinn, humankind and animals, for He will exact retribution on that day for the hornless sheep from the horned one, until no claim remains between one and another. Then God says: 'Be dust,' and at that the disbeliever says: 'Would that I were dust.' Then God, Glorified is He, judges between jinn and humankind."

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾: the rows of the angels.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And Hell is brought forth that Day﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: And God brings Hell forth that day.

As follows:

- Al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to us, he said: Marwan al-Fazari narrated to us, from al-Ala ibn Khalid al-Asadi, from Shaqiq ibn Salama, who said: Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said regarding His saying: ﴿And Hell is brought forth that Day﴾: It will be brought led by seventy thousand reins, with each rein seventy thousand angels leading it.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Asim ibn Bahdala, from Abu Wa'il: ﴿And Hell is brought forth that Day﴾: It will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, led by seventy thousand reins, with each rein seventy thousand angels.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, he said: Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: "Its two sides: Paradise and the Fire." He said: This is when He descends from His Throne to His Footstool for the reckoning of His creation, and he recited: ﴿And Hell is brought forth that Day﴾.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿And Hell is brought forth that Day﴾: It is brought bridled.

* *

And His saying: ﴿On that Day man will remember﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: On that day man will remember his neglect in the world regarding obedience to God and what brings him closer to Him of righteous deeds. ﴿But how will the remembrance benefit him?﴾ meaning: by what means will remembrance be for him?

And the people of interpretation said according to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, His saying: ﴿But how will the remembrance benefit him?﴾: he says: how for him

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 89, verse 24–30:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent forth [good] for my life!"﴾

Exalted is He, mentioning the regret and remorse of the son of Adam on the Day of Resurrection for his neglect, in the world, of the righteous deeds that would have earned him everlasting life in bliss that never ends: "Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life [in the world] the righteous deeds for this life of mine, which has no death after it, that would have saved me from the wrath of God and made His good pleasure due to me."

Those who gave interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Hawdhah related to us, saying: 'Awf related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿On that Day man will remember, but how will the remembrance benefit him? He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent forth [good] for my life!"﴾ He said: God knew that he was truthful; there is a long life there in which there is no death, the last thing upon him.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Oh, I wish I had sent forth [good] for my life!﴾ "There, by God, is the long life."

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Oh, I wish I had sent forth [good] for my life!﴾ He said: The Hereafter.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾

The readers of the cities (qurra' al-amsar) agreed on reading it with a kasra on the dhal of yu'adhdhibu and the tha' of yuthiqu, except al-Kisa'i, who read it with a fatha on the dhal and the tha', relying on a report narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he recited it that way, a report with a weak chain (wahi al-isnad).

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Kharijah, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, who said: Someone was related to me whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had taught to recite: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes﴾.

The correct view on this, in our opinion, is what the readers of the cities hold, namely the kasra on the dhal and the tha', because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it. Given that this is so, the meaning of the speech is: on that Day none will be punished with the punishment of God in the world, and none will be bound with His binding on that Day in the world. Likewise, those who read it that way among the people of interpretation understood it.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes﴾ and none will bind as God binds.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ He said: God knew that in the world there is punishment and binding, so He said: on that Day none will punish with His punishment in the world, and none will bind with His binding in the world.

As for the one who read it with a fatha, he directed its interpretation to: on that Day none in the world will punish as God punishes on that Day, and none in the world will bind as He binds on that Day. Some of the later readers who read it with a fatha interpreted it as: on that Day none will punish the punishment of the disbeliever, and none will bind the binding of the disbeliever. He said: How is the kasra permissible, when there is no one who punishes on that Day besides God? This interpretation is an error, because the people of interpretation explained it otherwise, together with the consensus of the authoritative readers upon reading it with the meaning that the interpretation of the people of interpretation brought. I do not think what led him to read it that way was anything but his unawareness of the correct way of interpreting it.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾

Exalted is He, mentioning the saying of the angels to His friends on the Day of Resurrection: "O tranquil soul" — by "tranquil" is meant the one that was reassured by God's promise which He made to the people of faith in the world, of honour in the Hereafter, and so it affirmed that.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ means: the one that affirms (al-musaddiqah).

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ it is the believer whose soul was reassured by what God promised.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: tranquil in what God said, and affirming what He said.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: the one that affirms, certain that God is its Lord, submitting to His command in what He does with it.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the soul that became certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart (dhara'a jash) for His command and obedience.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the one that turns penitently and humbly (al-munibah al-mukhbitah), that has become certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿al-Mutma'innah﴾ He said: the humble (al-mukhbitah) and the one tranquil in God.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the one that became certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih related to us, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the humble (al-mukhbitah).

* Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi related to me, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the one that became certain of meeting God, and steadied its heart for Him.

It is mentioned that in the recitation of Ubayy it is: ﴿O secure soul (al-amanah)﴾.

Mention of the transmission of that:

* Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, from Harun al-Qari, who said: Hilal related to me, from Abu Shaykh al-Hannai, regarding the recitation of Ubayy: ﴿O secure soul, the tranquil﴾. Al-Kalbi said: The secure (al-amanah) in this place means: the believing woman (al-mu'minah).

It was also said: this is the saying of the angel to the servant at the departure of his soul, giving him the good news of his Lord's pleasure with him, and the preparation of the honour which He has readied for him in His presence.

Mention of those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: It was recited: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), and Abu Bakr said: Indeed this is good. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the angel will say it to you at death."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih: ﴿Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ He said: this is at death. ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: this is on the Day of Resurrection.

Others said regarding that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Usamah ibn Zayd, from his father, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: it was given the good news of Paradise at death, and on the Day of Gathering, and at the Resurrection.

* * *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: This is a report from God, exalted is His praise, of the saying of the angels to the soul of the believer at the Resurrection, commanding it to return into the body of its owner. They said: What is meant by "return" here is its owner.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ He said: The tranquil spirits will be returned into the bodies on the Day of Resurrection.

* It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants and enter My Paradise﴾: God commands the spirits on the Day of Resurrection to return to the bodies, and they come to God as He created them the first time.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, from 'Ikrimah regarding this verse: ﴿Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾: to the body.

Others said: Rather, that is said to it at death.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih: ﴿Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ He said: this is at death. ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: this is on the Day of Resurrection.

The more correct of the two views, in our judgment, is the view we have mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak: that this is said to them at the return of the spirits into the bodies on the Day of Resurrection, as indicated by His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants and enter My Paradise﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: the meaning is: enter among My righteous servants, and enter My Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: enter among My righteous servants ﴿and enter My Paradise﴾.

Others said: the meaning of that is: enter into My obedience and enter My Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Nu'aym ibn Damdam, from Muhammad ibn Muzahim, brother of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: into My obedience. ﴿And enter My Paradise﴾ He said: into My mercy.

Some of the grammarians of Basra directed the meaning of His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ to: enter into my party (hizb).

Some of the grammarians of Kufa interpreted that ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ as: with faith and affirmation of the reward and resurrection, "return" — the angels say to them, when their books are given to them in their right hands: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, to what God has prepared for you of reward. He said: It may also be that they say to them, something similar to this, intending: "Return from the world to this place of return." He said: You say to a man, "Where are you from?" and he says, "A Mudari," and you say, "Be a Tamimi or a Qaysi," meaning: you are from one of these two. So "be" here is a connective (silah), and likewise "return" is a connective, since he has already arrived at the Day of Resurrection, so the command has the meaning of a statement, as if He said: "O soul, you are well-pleased and well-pleasing."

It has been related from some of the early generation that he used to recite it: ﴿So enter among My servant (fi 'abdi) and enter My Paradise﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Harun, from Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Sulayman ibn Qatta, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited it: ﴿So enter among My servant (fi 'abdi)﴾ in the singular.

* Khallad ibn Aslam related to me, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, from Harun al-Qari, who said: Hilal related to me, from Abu al-Shaykh al-Hannai: ﴿fi 'abdi﴾. And in the saying of al-Kalbi: ﴿So enter among My servant and enter into My Paradise﴾, meaning: the spirit returns into the body.

The correct recitation regarding this is ﴿So enter among My servants﴾, meaning: enter among My righteous servants, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

They said: What is meant by "return" here is its owner.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ He said: The tranquil spirits will be returned into the bodies on the Day of Resurrection.

* It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants and enter My Paradise﴾: God commands the spirits on the Day of Resurrection to return to the bodies, and they come to God as He created them the first time.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, from 'Ikrimah regarding this verse: ﴿Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾: to the body.

Others said: Rather, that is said to it at death.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih: ﴿Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ He said: this is at death. ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: this is on the Day of Resurrection.

The more correct of the two views, in our judgment, is the view we have mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak: that this is said to them at the return of the spirits into the bodies on the Day of Resurrection, as indicated by His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants and enter My Paradise﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: the meaning is: enter among My righteous servants, and enter My Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: enter among My righteous servants ﴿and enter My Paradise﴾.

Others said: the meaning of that is: enter into My obedience and enter My Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Nu'aym ibn Damdam, from Muhammad ibn Muzahim, brother of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: into My obedience. ﴿And enter My Paradise﴾ He said: into My mercy.

Some of the grammarians of Basra directed the meaning of His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ to: enter into my party (hizb).

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Kharijah, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, who said: Someone was related to me whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had taught to recite: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes﴾.

The correct view on this, in our opinion, is what the readers of the cities hold, namely the kasra on the dhal and the tha', because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it. Given that this is so, the meaning of the speech is: on that Day none will be punished with the punishment of God in the world, and none will be bound with His binding on that Day in the world. Likewise, those who read it that way among the people of interpretation understood it.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes﴾ and none will bind as God binds.

I do not think what led him to read it that way was anything but his unawareness of the correct way of interpreting it.

Mention of those who said that:

* 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ means: the one that affirms (al-musaddiqah).

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ it is the believer whose soul was reassured by what God promised.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: tranquil in what God said, and affirming what He said.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: the one that affirms, certain that God is its Lord, submitting to His command in what He does with it.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the soul that became certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart (dhara'a jash) for His command and obedience.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the one that turns penitently and humbly (al-munibah al-mukhbitah), that has become certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿al-Mutma'innah﴾ He said: the humble (al-mukhbitah) and the one tranquil in God.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the one that became certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih related to us, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the humble (al-mukhbitah).

* Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi related to me, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the one that became certain of meeting God, and steadied its heart for Him.

It is mentioned that in the recitation of Ubayy it is: ﴿O secure soul (al-amanah)﴾.

Mention of the transmission of that:

* Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, from Harun al-Qari, who said: Hilal related to me, from Abu Shaykh al-Hannai, regarding the recitation of Ubayy: ﴿O secure soul, the tranquil﴾. Al-Kalbi said: The secure (al-amanah) in this place means: the believing woman (al-mu'minah).

Others said regarding that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Usamah ibn Zayd, from his father, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: it was given the good news of Paradise at death, and on the Day of Gathering, and at the Resurrection.

They said: What is meant by "return" here is its owner.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ He said: The tranquil spirits will be returned into the bodies on the Day of Resurrection.

* It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants and enter My Paradise﴾: God commands the spirits on the Day of Resurrection to return to the bodies, and they come to God as He created them the first time.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, from 'Ikrimah regarding this verse: ﴿Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾: to the body.

Others said: Rather, that is said to it at death.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih: ﴿Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ He said: this is at death. ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: this is on the Day of Resurrection.

The more correct of the two views, in our judgment, is the view we have mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak: that this is said to them at the return of the spirits into the bodies on the Day of Resurrection, as indicated by His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants and enter My Paradise﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: the meaning is: enter among My righteous servants, and enter My Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: enter among My righteous servants ﴿and enter My Paradise﴾.

Others said: the meaning of that is: enter into My obedience and enter My Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Nu'aym ibn Damdam, from Muhammad ibn Muzahim, brother of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: into My obedience. ﴿And enter My Paradise﴾ He said: into My mercy.

Some of the grammarians of Basra directed the meaning of His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ to: enter into my party (hizb).

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Kharijah, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, who said: Someone was related to me whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had taught to recite: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes﴾.

The correct view on this, in our opinion, is what the readers of the cities hold, namely the kasra on the dhal and the tha', because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it. Given that this is so, the meaning of the speech is: on that Day none will be punished with the punishment of God in the world, and none will be bound with His binding on that Day in the world. Likewise, those who read it that way among the people of interpretation understood it.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes﴾ and none will bind as God binds.

I do not think what led him to read it that way was anything but his unawareness of the correct way of interpreting it.

Mention of those who said that:

* 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ means: the one that affirms (al-musaddiqah).

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ it is the believer whose soul was reassured by what God promised.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: tranquil in what God said, and affirming what He said.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: the one that affirms, certain that God is its Lord, submitting to His command in what He does with it.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the soul that became certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart (dhara'a jash) for His command and obedience.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the one that turns penitently and humbly (al-munibah al-mukhbitah), that has become certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿al-Mutma'innah﴾ He said: the humble (al-mukhbitah) and the one tranquil in God.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the one that became certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih related to us, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the humble (al-mukhbitah).

* Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi related to me, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the one that became certain of meeting God, and steadied its heart for Him.

It is mentioned that in the recitation of Ubayy it is: ﴿O secure soul (al-amanah)﴾.

Mention of the transmission of that:

* Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, from Harun al-Qari, who said: Hilal related to me, from Abu Shaykh al-Hannai, regarding the recitation of Ubayy: ﴿O secure soul, the tranquil﴾. Al-Kalbi said: The secure (al-amanah) in this place means: the believing woman (al-mu'minah).

Others said regarding that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Usamah ibn Zayd, from his father, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: it was given the good news of Paradise at death, and on the Day of Gathering, and at the Resurrection.

Some of them said: This is a report from God, exalted is His praise, of the saying of the angels to the soul of the believer at the Resurrection, commanding it to return into the body of its owner. They said: What is meant by "return" here is its owner.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ He said: The tranquil spirits will be returned into the bodies on the Day of Resurrection.

* It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants and enter My Paradise﴾: God commands the spirits on the Day of Resurrection to return to the bodies, and they come to God as He created them the first time.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, from 'Ikrimah regarding this verse: ﴿Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾: to the body.

Others said: Rather, that is said to it at death.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih: ﴿Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ He said: this is at death. ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: this is on the Day of Resurrection.

The more correct of the two views, in our judgment, is the view we have mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak: that this is said to them at the return of the spirits into the bodies on the Day of Resurrection, as indicated by His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants and enter My Paradise﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: the meaning is: enter among My righteous servants, and enter My Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: enter among My righteous servants ﴿and enter My Paradise﴾.

Others said: the meaning of that is: enter into My obedience and enter My Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Nu'aym ibn Damdam, from Muhammad ibn Muzahim, brother of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: into My obedience. ﴿And enter My Paradise﴾ He said: into My mercy.

Some of the grammarians of Basra directed the meaning of His saying: ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ to: enter into my party (hizb).

Some of the grammarians of Kufa interpreted that ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ as: with faith and affirmation of the reward and resurrection, "return" — the angels say to them, when their books are given to them in their right hands: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, to what God has prepared for you of reward. He said: It may also be that they say to them, something similar to this, intending: "Return from the world to this place of return." He said: You say to a man, "Where are you from?" and he says, "A Mudari," and you say, "Be a Tamimi or a Qaysi," meaning: you are from one of these two. So "be" here is a connective (silah), and likewise "return" is a connective, since he has already arrived at the Day of Resurrection, so the command has the meaning of a statement, as if He said: "O soul, you are well-pleased and well-pleasing."

It has been related from some of the early generation that he used to recite it: ﴿So enter among My servant (fi 'abdi) and enter My Paradise﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Harun, from Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Sulayman ibn Qatta, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited it: ﴿So enter among My servant (fi 'abdi)﴾ in the singular.

* Khallad ibn Aslam related to me, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, from Harun al-Qari, who said: Hilal related to me, from Abu al-Shaykh al-Hannai: ﴿fi 'abdi﴾. And in the saying of al-Kalbi: ﴿So enter among My servant and enter into My Paradise﴾, meaning: the spirit returns into the body.

The correct recitation regarding this is ﴿So enter among My servants﴾, meaning: enter among My righteous servants, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Fajr.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 89, verse 24–30:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent forth [good] for my life!"﴾

Exalted is He, mentioning the regret and remorse of the son of Adam on the Day of Resurrection for his neglect, in the world, of the righteous deeds that would have earned him everlasting life in bliss that never ends: "Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life [in the world] the righteous deeds for this life of mine, which has no death after it, that would have saved me from the wrath of God and made His good pleasure due to me."

Those who gave interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Hawdhah related to us, saying: 'Awf related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿On that Day man will remember, but how will the remembrance benefit him? He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent forth [good] for my life!"﴾ He said: God knew that he was truthful; there is a long life there in which there is no death, the last thing upon him.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Oh, I wish I had sent forth [good] for my life!﴾ "There, by God, is the long life."

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Oh, I wish I had sent forth [good] for my life!﴾ He said: The Hereafter.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾

The readers of the cities (qurra' al-amsar) agreed on reading it with a kasra on the dhal of yu'adhdhibu and the tha' of yuthiqu, except al-Kisa'i, who read it with a fatha on the dhal and the tha', relying on a report narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he recited it that way, a report with a weak chain (wahi al-isnad).

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Kharijah, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, who said: Someone was related to me whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had taught to recite: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes﴾.

The correct view on this, in our opinion, is what the readers of the cities hold, namely the kasra on the dhal and the tha', because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it. Given that this is so, the meaning of the speech is: on that Day none will be punished with the punishment of God in the world, and none will be bound with His binding on that Day in the world. Likewise, those who read it that way among the people of interpretation understood it.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes﴾ and none will bind as God binds.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ He said: God knew that in the world there is punishment and binding, so He said: on that Day none will punish with His punishment in the world, and none will bind with His binding in the world.

As for the one who read it with a fatha, he directed its interpretation to: on that Day none in the world will punish as God punishes on that Day, and none in the world will bind as He binds on that Day. Some of the later readers who read it with a fatha interpreted it as: on that Day none will punish the punishment of the disbeliever, and none will bind the binding of the disbeliever. He said: How is the kasra permissible, when there is no one who punishes on that Day besides God? This interpretation is an error, because the people of interpretation explained it otherwise, together with the consensus of the authoritative readers upon reading it with the meaning that the interpretation of the people of interpretation brought. I do not think what led him to read it that way was anything but his unawareness of the correct way of interpreting it.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾

Exalted is He, mentioning the saying of the angels to His friends on the Day of Resurrection: "O tranquil soul" — by "tranquil" is meant the one that was reassured by God's promise which He made to the people of faith in the world, of honour in the Hereafter, and so it affirmed that.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ means: the one that affirms (al-musaddiqah).

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ it is the believer whose soul was reassured by what God promised.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: tranquil in what God said, and affirming what He said.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: the one that affirms, certain that God is its Lord, submitting to His command in what He does with it.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the soul that became certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart (dhara'a jash) for His command and obedience.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the one that turns penitently and humbly (al-munibah al-mukhbitah), that has become certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿al-Mutma'innah﴾ He said: the humble (al-mukhbitah) and the one tranquil in God.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the one that became certain that God is its Lord, and steadied its heart for His command.

* Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih related to us, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the humble (al-mukhbitah).

* Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi related to me, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: the one that became certain of meeting God, and steadied its heart for Him.

It is mentioned that in the recitation of Ubayy it is: ﴿O secure soul (al-amanah)﴾.

Mention of the transmission of that:

* Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, from Harun al-Qari, who said: Hilal related to me, from Abu Shaykh al-Hannai, regarding the recitation of Ubayy: ﴿O secure soul, the tranquil﴾. Al-Kalbi said: The secure (al-amanah) in this place means: the believing woman (al-mu'minah).

It was also said: this is the saying of the angel to the servant at the departure of his soul, giving him the good news of his Lord's pleasure with him, and the preparation of the honour which He has readied for him in His presence.

Mention of those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: It was recited: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), and Abu Bakr said: Indeed this is good. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the angel will say it to you at death."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih: ﴿Return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ He said: this is at death. ﴿So enter among My servants﴾ He said: this is on the Day of Resurrection.

Others said regarding that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Usamah ibn Zayd, from his father, regarding His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ He said: it was given the good news of Paradise at death, and on the Day of Gathering, and at the Resurrection.
